characters.notes:
* Tainted Isaac can only hold 8 passive items at a time. Tainted Isaac's current 8 passive items are visible in the top-left corner of the screen, with one highlighted by a white square. Upon picking up a 9th passive item, the item currently selected, or rather the item currently in the white square, will be dropped on a pedestal in front of Tainted Isaac. The swap key can be pressed to cycle which item is selected.
* In exchange for this, all rerollable item pedestals, ⟦pool:Shop¦Shop items⟧, and ⟦pool:Devil Room¦Devil deals⟧ will cycle between two items for the player to choose from, essentially a stronger version of ⟦i:414¦More Options⟧ + ⟦i:249¦There's Options⟧. Whichever item is currently visible when the item is picked up will be the one selected. Once an item has been picked up it will no longer cycle between items.
* ⟦i:327¦The Polaroid⟧, ⟦i:328¦The Negative⟧, ⟦i:238¦Key Piece 1⟧, ⟦i:239¦Key Piece 2⟧, ⟦i:626¦Knife Piece 1⟧, ⟦i:627¦Knife Piece 2⟧, ⟦i:668¦Dad's Note⟧, ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧, the passive item created when ⟦i:577¦Damocles⟧ is used (the one with item ID 656), and all activated items are exempt from this limit and do not take up inventory space. Swallowed trinkets also do not count towards the 8 item limit.
* Dropping items causes their passive buffs to be removed, however health or pickups will be kept (such as from⟦i:25¦Breakfast⟧ or ⟦i:141¦Pageant Boy⟧). Note that pickups will be kept regardless of which way they were gained (picked up or directly added to the counters).
* Even if one of the item is a set drop, the other one is still randomly pulled from the current room's item pool.
characters.strategy:
* While most passive items have their effects "bound" to them, with the changes reverted with the loss of the item, some passive items have a permanent effect that triggers on pickup. HP upgrades like ⟦i:25¦Breakfast⟧, and pickup spawners like ⟦i:141¦Pageant Boy⟧ can all be left behind immediately. Many items not having their effects reverted are listed in Synergies and Interactions section.
** Rerolled health items makes Tainted Isaac lose the health "bound". Using the ⟦i:284¦D4⟧ or ⟦i:283¦D100⟧ or ⟦i:489¦D infinity⟧ to reroll passive items then dropping gained health items makes it easier for him to accumulate more health containers.
* Stat changes from Pills are permanent. This can make them either extremely useful or dangerous, as high natural stats mean less need to carry stat up items, but Tainted Isaac cannot counteract stat downs with items as easily due to the limited inventory.
* Due to the limited amount of items, Trinkets have a more important role with this character. Therefore any item helping to gain some, such as ⟦i:439¦Mom's Box⟧, will help a lot. Items or pickups that allow to absorb them (⟦i:538¦Marbles⟧, ⟦i:479¦Smelter⟧, Gulp!...) are even more important as absorbed trinkets do not take up an item slot.
* Transformations are permanent, and the progress towards transformations by passive items remains if it is replaced with a new item.
** Transformation progress of an item will be lost if the passive item is removed in any other way, such as being rerolled with⟦i:284¦D4⟧, or destroyed by ⟦i:536¦Sacrificial Altar⟧
* Items that would add items directly to Tainted Isaac (such as ⟦i:412¦Cambion Conception⟧, ⟦i:123¦Monster Manual⟧, etc) or pickups that would do the same (such as ⟦p:soul-of-lilith¦Soul of Lilith⟧) do not take up an inventory slot.
** If ⟦p:soul-of-lilith¦Soul of Lilith⟧ is used while Tainted Isaac has an empty slot, the familiar granted by the soul will take up the slot and can be dropped in exchange for another item as normal.
* On item choice, instead of building up stats, it's more effective to find and optimize strong synergies.
* In Co-op mode, the other character can pick up the items that Tainted Isaac drops but this item will no longer contribute to the transformation it is a part of.
** Killing the Boss of a floor in Co-op mode will spawn a Boss item that cycles between two different options, but any subsequent options will not come with an extra choice.
* Cards like ⟦p:xiv-temperance¦XIV - Temperance⟧ or ⟦p:xx-judgement¦XX - Judgement⟧ can be extremely powerful, as they allow to spawn an item from a specific item pool. For example, donating to a Blood Donation Machine will spawn either ⟦i:119¦Blood Bag⟧ or ⟦i:135¦IV Bag⟧ and cycle with a second item pulled from the current room item pool. This can be used to get powerful items from Angel / Devil Room, or help in completing the collection page if the player wishes to avoid a full game break (such as using ⟦c:tainted-cain¦Tainted Cain⟧ or ⟦i:166¦D20⟧) and is actively looking for items in a specific pool.
* Similar to the above, ⟦p:vi-the-lovers-reversed¦VI - The Lovers?⟧, ⟦p:viii-justice-reversed¦VIII - Justice?⟧ and ⟦p:xvii-the-stars-reversed¦XVII - The Stars?⟧ allow the generation of items from a specific pool, directly through ⟦p:vi-the-lovers-reversed¦VI - The Lovers?⟧ and ⟦p:xvii-the-stars-reversed¦XVII - The Stars?⟧, and indirectly through the golden chests spawned by ⟦p:viii-justice-reversed¦VIII - Justice?⟧ if they happen to contain items.

tips: Choisissez soigneusement ce que vous gardez : chaque emplacement compte.

characters.notes:
* When Tainted Magdalene's health is above 2 Red Hearts, she will leave red creep on the floor and will lose health at the rate of half a heart per 10 seconds. This health loss affects all types of hearts, but prioritizes red heart health. Affected hearts on the health bar are faded and slowly pulsating.
** Bone Hearts are drained, although empty ones will not be broken by the drain effect.
** All leaking hearts, including red ones, will protect against loss of Devil Room/Angel Room chances; only non-leaky red heart damage will impose a penalty.
** Her first two Red Heart containers as well as Rotten Hearts and Eternal Hearts are the only hearts that do not leak. When Tainted Magdalene has only Soul Hearts, they will continuously leak until she has half a soul heart left.
* She also receives double healing from all sources except heart pickups, and all enemies have a chance of dropping a Half Red Heart upon death which will flicker and disappear in 2 seconds.
* Tainted Magdalene has a distinctive melee attack which is automatically performed on enemies who make contact with her. The "hug" is a swing that functions similarly to ⟦c:the-forgotten¦The Forgotten⟧'s Bone Club, and can synergize with any held items. Melee hits deal 6× damage and all enemies killed by the melee attack have a 100% chance of dropping a half red heart.
* The Ace cards will transform the half red hearts, which would normally flicker and disappear, into normal consumables. Using them after killing a lot of enemies with the melee ability can be a good way to get a large amount of consumables. Consumables rerolled into by ⟦i:166¦D20⟧ or ⟦i:405¦GB Bug⟧ will still flicker and disappear.
* One Rotten Heart will provide two Rotten hearts upon pickup.
* Half red hearts affected by ⟦p:jera¦Jera⟧ will not disappear. It is unknown whether this behavior is intentional or not.
characters.strategy:
Tainted Magdalene's strength comes from having very expendable health in the early game. Her ability to regenerate Red Hearts from slain foes allows for simply charging into groups of enemies and killing them all with her lethal hugs. With the invincibility frames that come with taking damage, she can not only sustain but actually gain health from hugging enemies during the invincibility period. This can result in massive health gain from large groups of fragile, easily slain enemies.
These advantages come at the cost of her base damage, which is significantly lower than other characters at a permanent 0.75× multiplier. Items that increase damage should be high priority, so that she may remain effective later in the run.
As Soul Heart/Black Hearts will drain just like Red Hearts do, they are generally less useful as Tainted Magdalene. This is compounded by the fact that her leaky red hearts already protect against the loss of a Devil Room/Angel Room chance.
Whilst she excels against groups of weak enemies, Tainted Magdalene suffers against high-health enemies as well as bosses that don't summon many enemies, such as ⟦e:delirium¦Delirium⟧. Unless she can find a way to sustain her health pool for the fight, she will slowly lose health until she is down to her 2 permanent red hearts.
can cause more trouble for Tainted Magdalene than for other characters, as knowing how much health she has is important. She stops producing red creep when she runs out of leaky red hearts, which may be a helpful indicator.

weaknesses: Ses cœurs temporaires se vident avec le temps

characters.notes:
* Tainted Cain can't obtain items through any means other than the Bag of Crafting, and attempting to take an item from a pedestal will reduce it to an assortment of pickups.
* The pickups dropped are dependent on what type of room the item was touched in; Items touched in Secret Rooms will drop Bone Hearts, Curse Rooms will create Rotten Hearts, Planetariums will spawn Runes, Devil Rooms/Angel Rooms will cause items to generate Black Hearts/Eternal Hearts, ⟨16⟩ and items from Ultra Secret Rooms will drop ⟦p:cracked-key¦Cracked Key⟧s respectively. Crafting an active item when already holding one will also transform the old active item into random consumables instead of dropping it.
* Almost all crafting recipes are seeded and are random per run.
* The order of the ingredients does not matter.
* Half Red Heart/Half Soul Heart counts as one heart in terms of crafting.
* Blended Heart counts as one red heart plus one soul heart.
* Double Bombs, Double Hearts, and Double Pennies count as two of the individual item rather than being distinct items.
* Lucky Pennies and Golden Pennies are distinct from both themselves and from Pennies.
* Charged Keys are distinct from Keys.
* If a mod is installed and enabled that adds new items in any form, the Bag of Crafting's recipes shift entirely to accommodate for their presence. This renders guides on exact recipes inaccurate.
* Items related to story plots are not affected and can be taken as normal, including:
** ⟦i:327¦The Polaroid⟧
** ⟦i:328¦The Negative⟧
** ⟦i:238¦Key Piece 1⟧
** ⟦i:239¦Key Piece 2⟧
** ⟦i:550¦Broken Shovel 1⟧
** ⟦i:551¦Broken Shovel 2⟧
** ⟦i:552¦Mom's Shovel⟧
** ⟦i:668¦Dad's Note⟧
** ⟦i:633¦Dogma⟧
** ⟦i:626¦Knife Piece 1⟧
** ⟦i:627¦Knife Piece 2⟧
* Items are not removed from item pools upon being turned into pickups, nor from being successfully crafted. However, seeing an item still applies weight decrementation.
* Items that cannot be crafted include:
** ⟦i:73¦Cube of Meat⟧
** ⟦i:207¦Ball of Bandages⟧
** ⟦i:293¦Head of Krampus⟧
** ⟦i:132¦A Lump of Coal⟧
** ⟦i:130¦A Pony⟧
** ⟦i:181¦White Pony⟧
** ⟦i:710¦Bag of Crafting⟧
** Other items that exclusively drop from specific bosses or machines.
** ⟦i:474¦Broken Glass Cannon⟧
** ⟦i:714¦Recall⟧ and ⟦i:715¦Hold⟧.
* As with his regular counterpart ⟦c:cain¦Cain⟧, Tainted Cain can only shoot tears from his right eye, and as such shares all the same item interactions.
characters.strategy:
As Tainted Cain has "No Destiny", he must create his own with the Bag of Crafting. While it is tempting to place pickups like coins and health into the Bag of Crafting as soon as they are encountered, this will likely only lead to the creation of lower-quality items. Tainted Cain rewards players who use lower-valued pickups in a way that helps them obtain higher-valued ones in order to craft powerful items.
* It is strongly advised to unlock most if not all pickups prior to playing Tainted Cain. High-tier items become much harder or even impossible to craft without certain unlockable pickups, such as Bone Hearts.
* Many alternate ways of getting pedestal items, such as Shops or Devil Rooms, become irrelevant or outright detrimental when playing as Tainted Cain. Taking a Devil Deal only has the immediate benefit of dropping Black Hearts, which in general are more beneficial to find through other means, such as Curse Rooms. As such, it is often more beneficial to skip the first Devil Room and instead potentially get free materials from a later Angel Room.
** Shop items can still be purchased by swiping them up with the Bag of Crafting, making them a consistent source of more remarkable ingredients.
* Cards (and pills) may want to be checked for their effects before having them put in the Bag of Crafting, as a few may be more beneficial to use as themselves than to use as part of a recipe.
* It may be effective to leave room rewards and pedestal item drops for a later time, then return to craft items out of the more expensive materials once more are gathered.
* Items across pits and rocks that would otherwise require resources or would be unobtainable can usually be grabbed by the Bag of Crafting's swing range.
* It is possible, with the crafting of 4x ⟦i:636¦R Key⟧s, to get every Completion Mark in a single run, except the ones for ⟦s:greed-mode¦Greed Mode⟧.

characters.notes:
* When used, Dark Arts gives Tainted Judas +1.0 speed and makes him invulnerable to damage for a short period of time. Any enemies touched while Dark Arts is active will be frozen until the effect ends, at which point they will take damage (x2.5 your damage + 3.5 flat damage). Any enemy projectiles touched while Dark Arts is active will be destroyed. At the end of the effect, a blast effect occurs. The total explosion damage dealt is proportional to the number of enemies touched, and each enemy killed or projectile destroyed grants Tainted Judas a temporary damage boost. The damage boost scales and lasts longer depending on the number of enemies killed and projectiles destroyed.
* Tainted Judas is unable to gain Red Hearts. Health Ups will give him Black Hearts instead. If he picks up a Bone Heart, he will be unable to fill it with red health.
characters.strategy:
* Tainted Judas is best suited to a highly aggressive playstyle; making effective use of Dark Arts by rushing into the fray and striking as many enemies as possible, then clearing up stragglers with buffed damage. However, it shouldn't be mistaken as a purely offensive tool, as the ability to destroy projectiles gives it great defensive utility when used properly. For example, timing its activation to cross through the origin point of a nova of bullets as they spawn simultaneously removes the need to dodge and grants a massive damage boost.
** It is vital to get a feel for how long Dark Arts remains active, as being inside an enemy or hazard when it ends will typically result in damage taken.
** Dark Arts can nullify a lot of the harder puzzle rooms, as one can walk straight through spikes and shots while it's active. In addition, being able to safely enter every Curse Room grants a risk-free opportunity to build up soul/black hearts or find powerful items every floor.
** Certain enemies or bosses that rapidly fire bullets, such as Soy Creeps, Revenants, ⟦e:baby-plum¦Baby Plum⟧, ⟦e:hush¦Hush⟧, etc. are a boon for Tainted Judas; as every bullet walked through contributes to the damage bonus, these can stack up extremely quickly, and as long as the enemy/boss remains alive, this can be repeated indefinitely. This can lead to obscene amounts of damage that can potentially last through an entire run.
* Tainted Judas is extremely effective in Greed Mode, due to the quick transitions between waves allowing for repeated use of Dark Arts to continue stacking damage and getting free Curse Rooms.
** Dark Arts can also be used to ignore the damage from the button and pause the timer for free.
* ⟨15⟩ Pay extra attention when fighting in the proximity of pickups like cards, pills and runes, as Tainted Judas may pick them up inadvertently and use them instead of Dark Arts when trying to rush through enemies, resulting in taking damage.

tips: Dark Arts est plus rentable quand il traverse plusieurs ennemis.

characters.notes:
* While playing as Tainted ???, bomb pickups are replaced by poop pickups, and his bomb counter is replaced by a poop counter which displays the number and effects of his poops. The order in which different types of poop are obtained is predetermined based on the seed. By default, Tainted ??? can carry a maximum of 10 poops: 9 in the poop counter and 1 in Hold.
* Using Hold will store his leftmost poop for later use and cycle to the next poop.
* Besides replacing bomb pickups, poop pickups also have a chance to drop from fallen enemies and from Tainted ??? by dealing damage. There are small and large variants of poop pickups: small poop pickups give one poop, and large poop pickups give three poops.
* Most items that affect bomb count will spawn blue flies when playing as Tainted ???. For example, ⟦p:2-of-clubs¦2 of Clubs⟧ and ⟦i:19¦Boom!⟧ will spawn 2 and 10 flies, respectively.
** ⟨15⟩ However, Bombs Are Key pills seem to give Tainted ??? bombs internally (assuming he had keys before using the pill), as using the pill again will give back the amount of keys that were originally carried. When bombs are obtained this way, they can be given to Bomb Bums, though the number of bombs is invisible.
* Items/effects that reroll pickups (such as ⟦i:166¦D20⟧, ⟦i:405¦GB Bug⟧, etc.) will also reroll poop pickups.
** ⟦p:ix-the-hermit-reversed¦IX - The Hermit?⟧ will not convert poop pickups into coins.
* Tainted ???'s poops cannot be used to bridge over gaps, unlike the poops from ⟦i:36¦The Poop⟧.
* In Co-Op, partners can pick up poop drops if they're alive and still add them to Tainted ???'s reserve.
* In Co-Op, a bomb counter will be displayed if one of the characters is not Tainted ???, despite him not usually being able to see it.
* In Co-Op, Tainted ??? can infinitely use Bomb Bums without taking away bombs from the other player's reserves.
* Tainted ??? is unable to give poop pickups to Bomb Bums in place of bombs.
* Tainted ???'s tears are colored brown; this is purely cosmetic.
characters.strategy:
* As Tainted ??? begins with a low tears stat, it is almost required to rely on poops in the early game. The player should not be scared to use poops, as Tainted ??? will naturally create many poops as he deals damage, especially in boss battles. However, it may be best to save more powerful poops or poop synergies, such as White Poops and brown creep, for more difficult situations such as boss battles.
** Tainted ???'s low tears also makes tears up items like ⟦i:341¦Torn Photo⟧ very beneficial.
* More than any other type of poop, it can be beneficial to use Hold on bomb poops for utility purposes, such as finding Secret Rooms or reaching pickups behind rocks.
** Alternatively, flaming poops can be used in conjunction with stinky poops/farts to blow things up without using bombs. The stinky poop/fart can be used next to what the player wants to blow up, then the flaming poop can be thrown at it to create an explosion. This can also be done by throwing stinky poops at a fire or flaming poop, though care must be taken as it is easy to get caught in the ensuing explosion if the player does not move out of the way quickly enough.
* If playing in ⟦s:greed-mode¦Greed Mode⟧, it's best to try to complete all waves in one sitting as exiting the main room will cause all poops and creep to disappear.
* Almost anything that resembles a fire can cause toxic clouds created by farts and Stinky Poop to explode. This includes Fire Places, fires shot by enemies (such as Candlers, Fire Worms, and Revenants), and fires created by Tainted ??? (such as with ⟦i:164¦The Candle⟧, ⟦i:495¦Ghost Pepper⟧, and ⟦i:616¦Bird's Eye⟧). Extra caution must be taken to stay away from gas clouds if playing with or around fires.
** ⟦i:640¦Urn of Souls⟧ is a notable exception to this.
** Stinky Poops can intentionally be thrown at blue/purple fireplaces to blow them up for the chance to gain Soul Hearts. Be careful not to destroy ⟦e:gabriel¦Angel statues⟧ next to them if they’re in an Angel Room if you do not wish to fight the angel.

tips: Gérez les crottes comme une ressource : elles offrent protection et effets variés.

characters.notes:
After holding down the fire button for 2 seconds, a blood clot familiar that shoots tears will spawn alongside her, starting with 15 HP when spawned and slowly decaying down to their minimum stats. Each time a blood clot is spawned, half a heart is drained, and this process can be repeated until Tainted Eve has half a heart of health remaining. Using Sumptorium will transform clots back into health, with excess clots moved to the ground next to her. Clots being transformed back into health damage enemies for 3× her current damage as they pass through them.
If every remaining clot is killed and Tainted Eve only has half a red heart left, she is granted a ⟦i:122¦Whore of Babylon⟧-like effect and begins to use Sumptorium as a weapon that functions similarly to ⟦i:114¦Mom's Knife⟧. Unlike a ⟦i:114¦Mom's Knife⟧, the sumptorium knife has no synergies with some items, such as ⟦i:678¦C Section⟧, ⟦i:704¦Berserk!⟧, ⟦i:114¦Mom's Knife⟧, ⟦i:168¦Epic Fetus⟧, ⟦i:579¦Spirit Sword⟧, or ⟦t:180¦Found Soul⟧. The effect lasts until Tainted Eve either gains health or summons a clot, though the effect will persist until the next room is entered. This effect can also be triggered if Tainted Eve summons a blood clot while having no others and is left with half a heart. While under this effect, any summoned blood clots will use a small Mom's Knife for the rest of the room.
characters.strategy:
* Tainted Eve's strength is proportional to how many blood clots she has: she is required to keep them around for protection, while at the same time protecting them from harm in order to keep her offense going. Because of this, her runs can go hot and cold depending on her items and drops.
* As she is heavily geared towards turning health into familiars, an abundance of heart drops of any sort can easily grant Tainted Eve impressive room-clearing abilities. The sheer amount of blood clots will cause her to have extreme damage (due to the amount of tears being fired) and multiple "bodyguards" to block her from enemy tears.
* Tainted Eve loses a significant amount of staying power if she has low health and few clots: she will be forced to either use her horrendous base tears, or create a small number of blood clots that may end up dying anyway, which is usually the case during the start of a run.
* While Tainted Eve's passive ability causes her to drain health, the player can avoid this by "tap firing" instead of holding down the fire button. This does not affect the firing speed of Tainted Eve or her clots, and also lets her keep some backup health in her heart containers in case the player is not confident about avoiding damage.
* To make the most use of hearts, backtrack and use every remaining heart drop to create new clots once a floor is clear, and bomb objects that can potentially drop hearts, such as Blood Donation Machines.
* If you are at full health, keep in mind to pick up/use any health-restoring items like ⟦i:119¦Blood Bag⟧ or Full Health pills after you create clots, as it will make use of any potentially wasted heals.
* Clots slowly lose health as they stay out, to the point they can be killed by a single enemy bullet. It is usually a good habit to absorb clots with ⟦i:713¦Sumptorium⟧ to refresh their health, to prevent Tainted Eve from losing large amounts of clots later on. Be mindful that it will take a significant amount of time to rebuild her army of clots, so plan ahead.
** Tainted Eve can only reabsorb as many red clots as she has heart containers; leftover clots will remain on field without their health refreshed. If she has a massive amount of red clots, this means she runs the risk of losing any clots she is unable to reabsorb.
* Due to Tainted Eve's dependency on her clots to provide a physical wall of protection, she has a few notable weaknesses:
** Chasing enemies that deal contact damage, especially jumping ones like Trites, are some of the earliest problems she will face, as they can walk through clots or jump directly onto Tainted Eve while she is building an offensive.
** Enemies with piercing/area of effect abilities (such as enemy ⟦i:118¦Brimstone⟧ beams or ⟦i:149¦Ipecac⟧ shots) can instantly vaporize a large group of her clots or hit her when she is at half a heart.
** Rooms with lots of obstacles can prove to be detrimental, as it can cause the clots to separate and make them more likely to take damage, as well as reducing Tainted Eve's damage output.
** Bullet hell enemies will slowly chip away at her clots if she is careless. Thus, endgame bosses such as ⟦e:delirium¦Delirium⟧ and ⟦e:hush¦Hush⟧ will usually be her hardest challenge, since Tainted Eve will start out strong, but can become completely helpless at the end without any clots.
* As she is able to control how many hearts she possesses in her health, Tainted Eve can:
** Easily make use of both types of Challenge Rooms.
** "Reserve" heart drops by turning them into clots, and then heal herself back up afterwards. This can allow her to use self-harm sources such as Sacrifice Room, Curse Room, and Blood Donation Machine more frequently.
** Activate items that require certain amounts of health, such as ⟦i:122¦Whore of Babylon⟧ and ⟦i:409¦Empty Vessel⟧, while having a backup source of health (her clots).
* ⟦s:greed-mode¦Greed Mode⟧ is difficult for Tainted Eve, as she can struggle to get momentum going on the first two floors. A strong start is one with a lot of health available. You want to generate as many clots as possible, so you can quickly kill each new enemy wave as it appears. A handful of clots with a mild Damage or Tears Up starting item is worse than a mass of clots with base stats, making items like ⟦i:16¦Raw Liver⟧ desirable in the first Silver Treasure Room. Before starting the boss waves, consider how many clots you still have. If you're only a bit low, don't be afraid to buy Red Hearts from the shop to replenish their numbers. If you're low on health, clots, and money, it may be worth activating the powerful Whore Of Babylon effect and trying to quickly kill the bosses that way. If you can survive the first two floors, and hopefully pick up some decent offensive items, then the rest of the run tends to be easier.
* It is generally not advised to collect Rotten Hearts as Tainted Eve, as any active Rotten clots will overwrite existing Red Health every time ⟦i:713¦Sumptorium⟧ is used. Over time, This will cause you to lose all excess Red clots, substantially hindering your DPS potential.
* If entering the abandoned area of the mines to collect ⟦i:627¦Knife Piece 2⟧, then the ability to create clots will still be active, but ⟦i:713¦Sumptorium⟧ will not be available. If you are low on health be careful not to create clots because you won't be able to absorb them until you exit.

characters.notes:
* Whenever Tainted Samson deals or takes damage, he will grow progressively more red. After reaching a certain point, he activates ⟦i:704¦Berserk!⟧ and gains +0.40 speed, ×0.5 then +2 fire rate, +3 flat damage, and will be restricted to using a jawbone melee weapon instead of his tears (similarly to ⟦c:the-forgotten¦The Forgotten⟧'s bone club) which deals 3× his damage stat with strikes, 1.5× on thrown attacks, and reflects enemy shots when swung. The berserk state only lasts for 5 seconds at start, which is shown on a timer above his head, but one second is added every time Tainted Samson kills an enemy. Killing enemies in this state also grants speed, in increments of +0.40, as well as brief invincibility to prevent damage from exploding enemies. The effect persists between rooms. If he runs out of health while in this state, he will survive with no hearts, giving the player a short time to find more hearts before dying when the timer runs out.
* Entering the berserk state requires dealing a base total of 120 damage, and increases by 40 for every next floor. Taking damage adds 10% of the required total.
characters.strategy:
* Tainted Samson's game-plan requires management of berserk mode. He plays like a standard character until berserk activates, which can then be used to shred through rooms of enemies. Being able to make full use of berserk is key for effective use of the character.
* Berserk's benefits are immense, as Tainted Samson gains significant boosts to his melee abilities and speed, and even allows him to survive with no hearts so long as he picks up health before berserk ends. This all comes with a significant downside: berserk forces Tainted Samson to focus on melee attacks, making his effective range very low and extremely high risk.
* Berserk is best suited for a heavily aggressive playstyle: as it runs out in five seconds, Tainted Samson should aim to enter a room, slay as many enemies as possible, and rush into the next to keep berserk up for as long as he can.
* Berserk mode's swings are capable of reflecting enemy tears. If a situation forces berserking Tainted Samson from attacking a long-distance target, this can be used as a method to attack back or avoid damage. Alternatively, having a high tear rate will allow Tainted Samson to simply generate a reflective wall between himself and the enemy.
* While the thrown melee weapon charges quite fast, it still takes precious time from berserk's five second time limit. The thrown weapon should only be used if Tainted Samson cannot reach his enemy.
* As berserk charges through damage dealt and taken, it will activate quicker if Tainted Samson has a high damage per second or constantly gets hit.
* When clearing rooms in berserk mode, it is recommended to ignore room drops until berserk ends to make the most use of its limited timer.
* Berserk mode's swing will knockback targets slightly, which can help keep chasing enemies at a safe distance.
* Like the Forgotten's bone club, range ups will affect berserk's melee range, and can be used to open distant chests or pick up items across small gaps.
* As berserk mode activates relatively easily, it can make it hard to actually use tears. Items that grant tear effects will see less effective use on Tainted Samson because of this.
* Items that grant tears up are exceptional for Tainted Samson, as berserk already grants a high tear multiplier. A high tears will result in incredibly fast swing speed, which will shred through both enemies and tears alike.
* If Berserk is active, Tainted Samson can take damage while in the temporary Lost form in Downpour II. Damage will be drawn from his health bar normally.
* Samson's melee attack can collect pickups and open chests. Opening a Mimic Chest this way deals no damage. Locked Chests still require a key to open.

weaknesses: Le Berserk dépend d'une jauge, pas toujours disponible au bon moment
tips: Enchaînez les éliminations pendant le Berserk.

characters.notes:
* At the start of charging the ⟦i:118¦Brimstone⟧ attack, Azazel will fire ⟦i:726¦Hemoptysis⟧, causing a short-range, high-knockback "sneeze" attack that will curse enemies hit with a small Brimstone icon that hovers above its head and deal 1.5× damage. Hitting enemies with the Hemoptysis sneeze halves Brimstone's remaining charge time. Enemies will also take damage when knocked into walls or obstacles, and deal damage when colliding with other enemies.
* Furthermore, enemies cursed by Hemoptysis will take full damage instead of half damage (and +3 flat damage after multipliers) from his Brimstone beam for approximately 5 seconds; if killed during this time with Brimstone, they will explode, dealing damage to nearby enemies and spreading the curse to them. The Brimstone curse also applies to any enemies spawned by an enemy already affected by the curse. For example, the enemies and bosses spawned by ⟦e:mom-s-heart¦Mom's Heart⟧ will also have the curse if Mom's Heart had the curse at the time.
* While the Brimstone curse appears and acts as a status effect, it can be applied infinitely to Bosses and ignores their status effect immunity cooldown.
* Unlike Azazel, Tainted Azazel's wings are clipped and, as such, he doesn't start with Flight.
* When Tainted Azazel dies in Co-op, his ghost will maintain his Brimstone and Hemoptysis abilities. The first is weakened by the damage debuff applied to ghostly players, and the second is weakened as it has a very small size when dead.
characters.strategy:
* Using the sneeze in tandem with Brimstone is vital to use Tainted Azazel properly. Doing so will at least make him attack twice as fast and at best cause massive damage to enemies, making the run's speed highly variable on how well the player administrates the attack.
* The sneeze can be used both defensively to push enemies away and shred them with the curse from afar and rejecting projectiles, but also pushing enemies to a wall or spikes will make them suffer high damage; the player should consider if it's better for the enemy to die right away or be pushed into enemies to pass the curse on.
* This translates into a highly offensive play style, chaining attacks started up close to enemies to charge the laser to soften enemies far away while walking closer to sneeze on them and repeat. This cycle is more evident with bosses, especially stationary ones like ⟦e:gurdy¦Gurdy⟧ and ⟦e:hush¦Hush⟧.
* Failing to connect the sneeze often means having to either charge a significantly slower and weaker Brimstone shot or be unable to start the charge waiting for the sneeze to cooldown, although a short time, can leave Tainted Azazel without self-defense options without aid from bombs or familiars and missing attacking opportunities, especially with highly mobile enemies like ⟦e:the-pile¦The Pile⟧ and ⟦e:delirium¦Delirium⟧.

characters.notes:
* ⟨16⟩ Unlike other characters, Tainted Lazarus' ⟦i:711¦Flip⟧ only requires 4 charges.
* Correctly managing the charges of ⟦i:711¦Flip⟧ to get items for both forms of Tainted Lazarus from Treasure Rooms, Shops, Devil Rooms, and Angel Rooms is very important, as grabbing every flipped item effectively doubles the power of Tainted Lazarus.
* The only way to access the ghostly form of an item generated by ⟦i:711¦Flip⟧ is by using it to switch forms. Re-entering the room with a different form of Tainted Lazarus does not flip the item pedestals. Making Tainted Lazarus switch form inside the room without using ⟦i:711¦Flip⟧ (for example, after fighting an angel in the Angel room), does not flip the item pedestals.
* Flipping between forms will effectively act as a room transition for certain items; in other words, flipping back in the same room will reset those items as if a new room had been entered.
* Items that grant extra lives (⟦i:81¦Dead Cat⟧, ⟦i:11¦1up!⟧, ⟦i:332¦Lazarus' Rags⟧, etc.) only affect the one who picks them up. If Dead Lazarus collects an extra life item, it can only activate when Dead Lazarus is the active character, and vice versa.
* When transforming into a different character (e.g. with ⟦i:482¦Clicker⟧), only the current form's items will be given to the new character.
* If one form of Tainted Lazarus is reduced to zero hearts while being in the transitioning phase of Flip, he will remain alive as the other form, but die as soon as he switches back. There is nothing the other form can do to prevent that death, unless you're playing co-op and being revived after a boss death; in greedier/greed mode you will be revived if another player kills the first boss wave fought, while in XL floors, it is the 2nd boss killed that allows for a player revival while you are in the T Lazarus form that is in a baby ghost familiar form, so it's recommended to plan rooms accordingly.
* Quest items are counted as both characters having them.
** ⟦i:327¦The Polaroid⟧ and ⟦i:328¦The Negative⟧ work on both Living Tainted Lazarus and Dead Tainted Lazarus, regardless of which picked them up.
** ⟦i:238¦Key Piece 1⟧ and ⟦i:239¦Key Piece 2⟧ will grant their Angel Room bonus to both characters, and will combine to a whole key even if the pieces are not on the same character.
** ⟦i:626¦Knife Piece 1⟧ and ⟦i:627¦Knife Piece 2⟧ will combine to a whole knife usable by both characters regardless of who has which piece.
** ⟦i:633¦Dogma⟧'s flight and stat bonuses are applied to both characters, but healing and Holy Mantle apply only to the active character when receiving it. Since forms change after defeating Dogma, and the item is bestowed after the cutscene, this means that the form that was not active to defeat Dogma will receive the healing and mantle effect.
* Temporary buffs such as ⟦i:126¦Razor Blade⟧ disappear when you switch from one character to the other. This is especially noticeable in Greed Mode.
** However, room buffs like I'm Drowsy, ⟦p:era-walk¦Era Walk⟧, and ⟦p:xi-strength-reversed¦XI - Strength?⟧ will stay in effect between flips. Any stat bonuses given are lost.
* Only the character that picks up an activated item first gets the progress for related transformations, so the player needs to be aware of what character needs the transformation progress.
* Tainted Lazarus takes a lot of micromanagement compared to most other characters. It can be difficult to accomplish simple tasks due to the forced switching between forms and ⟦i:711¦Flip⟧'s long charge time. Try to stay ahead of this, and pay close attention to what form is active and when they will shift. Something such as collecting an item from a Treasure Room or Curse Room can potentially go wrong if enemies happen to be inside, as when they are defeated, Tainted Lazarus will switch form. This can lead to an undesired item on one form, or a forced use of Flip.
** If an Angel Room has an item you would prefer on one form over the other, and Flip is not currently charged, using a bomb on the Angel Statue and fighting the Angel that spawns will make Tainted Lazarus flip upon the fight's completion. This does not flip the item, however.
** Challenge Rooms and Boss Rush will flip Tainted Lazarus every wave.
* Active items will recharge even when the other form is active. For example, it will take 3 rooms to charge an active item that requires 3 bars to charge, despite the fact that the flipped form doesn't have the same active item. This effectively allows him to double the active item slots.
* Tainted Lazarus's strength lies in his control over his health bars. Using Flip strategically can avoid death if one form is low, save a deal chance if one character only has Red Hearts.
* If one form of Tainted Lazarus has flight and a room is cleared while above usually inaccessible land, Tainted Lazarus will gain a temporary flight for the current room.
* Greed and Greedier Modes have the following interactions with Tainted Lazarus:
** Each completed wave swaps from one form of Tainted Lazarus to the other, which locks him in the flip animation for about a second. He cannot fire tears while in this animation.
** Temporary buffs, such as ⟦i:34¦The Book of Belial⟧ or ⟦p:xi-strength¦XI - Strength⟧, will disappear when switching from one character to the other.
** Clearing the room before ⟦e:ultra-greed¦Ultra Greed⟧ does not switch characters.
* Some items and trinkets with the lazarussharedglobal item tag are shared between both forms. This includes items that map parts of the floor such as ⟦i:21¦The Compass⟧, items that increase devil/angel deal chance such as ⟦i:260¦Black Candle⟧, and items/trinkets that spawn new or altered rooms on each floor such as ⟦i:599¦Voodoo Head⟧. Items that grant a shared effect and a stat boost (such as ⟦i:51¦Pentagram⟧, which grants a damage increase and increases devil deal chance), will not transfer the stat increases between forms.
* Items that affect room clear awards (for example, ⟦i:241¦Contract From Below⟧) work only when the character holding the item appears after clearing the room.
* ⟦i:64¦Steam Sale⟧ is not shared between the two.
* During ⟦e:dogma¦Dogma⟧ + ⟦e:the-beast¦The Beast⟧ fight, flips happen between each boss, including the Ultra Harbingers.
* While playing co-op, Tainted Lazarus will still swap between forms while dead; if one of Tainted Lazarus' forms dies while the other is alive, he will alternate between being a ghost baby and a normal character.
** To be able to revive the dead version of Tainted Lazarus, the player must enter the boss fight while being on the alive form of the character, as the flip takes place BEFORE the revive process.
* Clearing a room under the effects of Paralysis will keep Tainted Lazarus's current state instead of switching to his counterpart.
* Items that affect item generation (⟦i:402¦Chaos⟧, ⟦i:691¦Sacred Orb⟧, etc.) will only take effect when the character holding the item is the one that is present when an item is generated (for example if the form that does not have the item defeats the boss room, the item generated will be affected by ⟦i:402¦Chaos⟧ because Tainted Lazarus will swap forms and then the item will be generated).

characters.notes:
* ⟨15⟩ Items are guaranteed to re-roll into items from the item pool of the last generated item (i.e. If one were to enter every item-containing room without picking up the items, then entered, for example, an Angel Room, every item that was already spawned will reroll into angel deal items when Tainted Eden receives damage).
* ⟨15⟩ Entering an item-containing room without picking up the items, then spawning an item from a specific item pool (e. g. an ⟦pool:Angel Room¦angel item⟧ by using ⟦i:585¦Alabaster Box⟧, or a ⟦pool:Shop¦shop item⟧ via ⟦i:719¦Keeper's Box⟧, etc.) will cause every item that was already spawned to reroll into items from that item pool.
* Self-damage (Blood Donation Machines, Devil Beggars, Curse Rooms, etc.) will not trigger a re-roll. Fatal damage will also not trigger a reroll.
* Tainted Eden cannot reroll ⟦i:328¦The Negative⟧, ⟦i:327¦The Polaroid⟧, ⟦i:668¦Dad's Note⟧, ⟦i:577¦Damocles⟧, ⟦i:633¦Dogma⟧, ⟦i:238¦Key Piece 1⟧, ⟦i:239¦Key Piece 2⟧, ⟦i:626¦Knife Piece 1⟧, or ⟦i:627¦Knife Piece 2⟧.
** Note that ⟦i:258¦Missing No.⟧ can be re-rolled into, but can't be re-rolled out of.
** Glitched items can be re-rolled into either glitched items or normal items if Tainted Eden is not holding ⟦i:721¦TMTRAINER⟧. If it is holding TMTRAINER, they can re-roll into other glitched items. Glitched items not re-rolling into normal items will eventually stop being re-rolled.
* Powerful transformations such as are difficult to attain, as transformations are removed if the appropriate items are re-rolled.
** However, picking up active items will also counts as transformation progress, which allows and much easier to keep.
* If Gulp! pills or a ⟦i:479¦Smelter⟧ are available, absorbing trinkets makes them permanent. If possible, they should be discarded to avoid losing them to a re-roll while looking for better trinkets.
* If Tainted Eden re-rolls while holding two trinkets (such as from ⟦i:139¦Mom's Purse⟧ or ⟦i:458¦Belly Button⟧), the trinket in the second slot is dropped rather than re-rolled. The same case happens with active items and ⟦i:534¦Schoolbag⟧.
* Each roll is seeded. For instance, reverting a re-roll with ⟦i:422¦Glowing Hourglass⟧ then getting hit will always give Tainted Eden their Glowing Hourglass back.
* Since Cards and Pills are re-rolled on hit, Tainted Eden should pick up ⟦p:0-the-fool¦0 - The Fool⟧ before the fight with ⟦e:mom¦Mom⟧ and drop it at the beginning of the battle, so as to not lose it if they take damage, if they intend to use it to open .
* Multiple copies of an item will be re-rolled into different items.
characters.strategy:
* The re-rolls will easily remove health, but not restore it. This makes it risky to focus solely on Red Hearts or Soul Hearts, and a balanced approach is overall safer.
** There is no guarantee of consistency to Tainted Eden's health. While acquiring Soul or Black Hearts may be a good idea because they cannot be re-rolled away, there is a chance that Tainted Eden rerolls into a build with massive amounts of red health, causing the overflowing Soul health to irrevocably disappear.
** It's not a good idea to get full 12 hearts. Having 6-9 hearts and leaving some hearts on ground to take when needed is much safer.
** is also potentially dangerous if one gets hit a lot, as your health is truly unknown.
** Since both getting and losing Heart Containers easily happen, it could be a good strategy to turn temporary Heart Containers into other resources whenever possible (by making devil deals or using both ⟦i:133¦Guppy's Paw⟧ or ⟦i:487¦Potato Peeler⟧).
* Gaining Heart Containers from sources other than passive items, such as Health Up pills, ⟦i:296¦Converter⟧ or Eternal Hearts is beneficial, because those changes are not affected by Tainted Eden's mechanic.
** Try to remember how many heart containers are gained by these way before using them in devil deals or so.
* More than other characters, Tainted Eden benefits from quantity over quality of individual items since the items are likely to get re-rolled several times anyway. Obtaining as many passive items as possible means more items to re-roll and more chances for useful synergies.
* Getting items from more consistently positive item pools can make a big difference. In particular, ⟦pool:Angel Room¦Angel Room items⟧ and ⟦pool:Planetarium¦Planetarium items⟧ are high-quality on average.
** Remember to check Shop, as which may provide discounted items, and passive items in ⟦pool:Shop¦Shop item pool⟧ may be re-rolled into great items like ⟦i:246¦Blue Map⟧ or ⟦i:260¦Black Candle⟧, whose effects last for the current floor. ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧ can only be purchased in shops, it can't be obtained via a reroll.
** Passive ⟦pool:Secret Room¦Secret Room items⟧ can offer powerful synergies, but run the risk of re-rolling into ⟦i:258¦Missing No.⟧ and ⟦i:721¦TMTRAINER⟧, both of which are extremely detrimental to almost any run. To avoid ever getting the latter item, consider defeating ⟦e:the-beast¦The Beast⟧ last, as that's what unlocks it. However, while Secret Room passive items are very risky, active items are instead very useful to keep around, as they are generally powerful, and they can be re-rolled into ⟦i:636¦R Key⟧ or ⟦i:628¦Death Certificate⟧.
** Active ⟦pool:Devil Room¦Devil Room Items⟧ are also very useful to keep around, as which can be re-rolled into ⟦i:577¦Damocles⟧ or ⟦i:133¦Guppy's Paw⟧.
** Focusing heavily on Devil Room items and not relying on Red Heart Containers in the first place is a viable strategy if plentiful Soul Hearts are acquired.
* Carrying around a Trinket, even a useless one, carries the opportunity of re-rolling it into a very good one, such as ⟦t:39¦Cancer⟧ or ⟦t:92¦Cracked Crown⟧ and so on.
* Cards, Runes, and Pills that aren't useful at the moment but may be useful later should be left or dropped on the ground so as to not lose them if a re-roll occurs. They can always be picked up later.
* The Library can be powerful for Tainted Eden. If ⟦i:584¦Book of Virtues⟧ is acquired from a Library, it cannot be re-rolled away due to how Book of Virtues is the only passive item in the ⟦pool:Library¦Library item pool⟧.
* Holding ⟦t:88¦NO!⟧ when taking a hit will re-roll Tainted Eden's active item into a passive item, which may or may not be desired.
* Plenty of trinkets don't need to be held constantly to benefit from their effects, so dropping them when they aren't needed is often advisable. In particular, trinkets that affect level generation like ⟦t:111¦Bloody Crown⟧, ⟦t:152¦Telescope Lens⟧ and ⟦t:102¦Fragmented Card⟧ can be dropped in the starting room of each floor, and only returned to once ready to proceed to the next.
* After rerolling everything, check if rocks are destroyed when walking into them. Several effects grant the ability to walk into rocks to destroy them, such as ⟦i:314¦Thunder Thighs⟧ or ⟦i:302¦Leo⟧.
** Also check if there are any item that helps you find and/or open Secret Room and Super Secret Room, or destroy Rocks without using bombs.
* Whenever Tainted Eden gets ⟦i:84¦We Need To Go Deeper!⟧ or ⟦i:580¦Red Key⟧, try to get a Crawl Space/ Ultra Secret Room as soon as possible before they are re-rolled.

characters.strategy:
* Tainted Lilith's special attack method is not an item and cannot be rerolled.
* Because of the special attack, Tainted Lilith starts with many perks that other characters would heavily benefit from: the launched baby has high starting damage, piercing, and the ability to attack through obstacles. However, this comes at the cost of Tainted Lilith's tears being much harder to use since it is tied to her baby, and the baby's umbilical cord gives its launching attack limited range.
* Tainted Lilith's launched baby is enough to one/two-shot most starting enemies, while the tears it fires are comparatively hard to control. It is usually best to use the baby as a makeshift melee weapon for clearing rooms unless Tainted Lilith can find some useful tear modifiers.
* When launched, Gello deals 3× damage and is capable of pushing enemies and bosses away on contact, making it handy to simply hit enemies with Gello rather than its tears. As such, a high tear rate does wonders for Tainted Lilith, as this also increases how quickly Gello can be launched from her. However, an overly high tear rate could be detrimental, as spamming the special attack causes Gello to return before it can hit any enemy.
* If the situation calls for it, Gello's tears can be used to safely attack at a distance as an extension of Tainted Lilith. However, this does not usually have use apart from very large rooms since Gello goes through obstacles.
* The hitbox of her special attack persists between rooms, meaning that launching Gello right before entering a room can potentially hit an enemy there.
* For early floors, prioritize getting speed upgrades over other stats. While Gello gives Tainted Lilith strong attacking power, it has to be relaunched each time, and her problematic base speed allows chasing enemies to easily overwhelm her. Look to get items that increase speed and avoid those that lower it further.
* During later floors, prioritize tear upgrades or range over other stats. At that point, using tears becomes a priority, since some bosses like ⟦e:delirium¦Delirium⟧ are able to teleport constantly, making it hard to use Gello's launch attack on them. Tainted Lilith usually has to resort to Gello's tears to deal consistent damage to these bosses.
* Gello cannot collect pickups, but it can knock them around. This ability can be used to dislodge pickups that would normally require you to walk over spikes to get.
* In Repentance Co-Op, if she dies, her familiar acts as normal, but still suffers the same penalties as other characters in this form.
* Unlike other characters, ⟦i:360¦Incubus⟧'s damage is not reduced by 25% while playing as Tainted Lilith. ⟦c:lilith¦Lilith⟧ shares this trait.

characters.strategy:
* Tainted Keeper plays like a glass cannon: his ability to stockpile coins lets him purchase many more items per floor than most other characters, allowing him to potentially steamroll early floors. However, his two coin hearts (and very limited methods to increase max health) means he is unable to make many mistakes in comparison, especially for drawn-out boss fights without monster spawns.
* In the standard game mode, Shops are different and much better for Tainted Keeper. They do not require a Key and generally have increased stock available. At max level, they have eight items/pickups for sale, of which there will always be at least one ⟦pool:Shop¦Shop item⟧, one ⟦pool:Boss¦Boss Room item⟧, and two ⟦pool:Treasure Room¦Treasure Room items⟧. The other four terminals in the shop can be keys, bombs, cards, pills, trinkets (which will be sold for 5 cents), or more Shop/Treasure Room items.
** This shop can rarely be replaced by a better (or worse) variant: The better variant has 2-6 more shopkeepers, Urns scattered about, two Lucky Pennies, and one more random item/pickup for sale. The worse variant has only one random sale terminal, one Shopkeeper, some Poop, and a Fly.
** These improved shops do not appear in ⟦s:greed-mode¦Greed Mode⟧.
** Due to shops including ⟦pool:Treasure Room¦Treasure Room items⟧, it is usually best to skip Treasure Rooms for a Planetarium.
* Some items do not need to be paid for. These include:
** Mini-Boss drops.
** ⟦i:90¦The Small Rock⟧ if dropped from a tinted rock.
** Golden and Red Chest items.
** Items spawned by beggars and machines.
** Items spawned by other items, such as through ⟦i:490¦Eden's Soul⟧ or ⟦p:xvii-the-stars-reversed¦XVII - The Stars?⟧ card.
** Plot-related items, including ⟦i:327¦The Polaroid⟧, ⟦i:328¦The Negative⟧, ⟦i:238¦Key Piece 1⟧, ⟦i:239¦Key Piece 2⟧, ⟦i:626¦Knife Piece 1⟧, ⟦i:627¦Knife Piece 2⟧, and ⟦i:668¦Dad's Note⟧.
*** This also applies to drops generated from Angel Statues while holding ⟦t:123¦Filigree Feather⟧.
** Boss drops in ⟦s:the-void¦The Void⟧.
* Enemies spawned after entering the room (i.e. spawned by another enemy or spawned on later waves in Challenge Rooms) don't have a guaranteed coin drop.
** Spawned enemies will stop dropping coins after fights go on long enough such as with Boss Rush.
* Champion enemies and Mini-Bosses drop 2 coins on death.
* Bosses drop several coins.
** If the boss comprises multiple enemies (e.g. ⟦e:gurglings¦Gurglings⟧), each of them drops fewer coins.
** Most degraded bosses drop 3 coins, exceptions such as ⟦e:the-cage¦The Cage⟧ and ⟦e:monstro-ii¦Monstro II⟧ have regular boss coin drops.
** Coins dropped by bosses stay on the floor longer before disappearing.
* Boss Rush items must still be paid for, and doing so will start the event.
* A high speed stat can help pick up coins before they disappear.
* A high fire rate will increase reliability in killing groups of enemies, allowing for safer coin collection. However, as changes to the Tears stat are much less effective on fire rate at or below -0.77 Tears (see Tears for the exact calculations), Tainted Keeper will gain very little fire rate from his first 1.43 added Tears. After crossing this threshold, as Tainted Keeper fires 4 tears at a time with no multiplicative fire rate penalty, he can gain far more DPS from Tears than other characters.
** For reference, a Tears Up pill gives 0.35 tears. Assuming no other tears modifiers are taken, Tainted Keeper will gain 0.07, 0.09, 0.10, and 0.12 fire rate from his first four Tears Up pills, and 0.52 from his fifth; more than his first four combined.
** Items that directly add fire rate are very desirable for Tainted Keeper while his Tears stat is low.
* Because Tainted Keeper has to pay for all items, taking devil deals is often more powerful than taking Angel items. This is because taking one devil deal item will not despawn the other items, but only one item can be taken from an Angel room.
** The following items cost 30 coins to purchase:
* Like ⟦c:tainted-magdalene¦Tainted Magdalene⟧, Tainted Keeper can take advantage of his coin-healing ability by running into a hoard of enemies, picking up coins during his invincibility frames and healing in the process. This is effective if the player has contact-based items like ⟦i:13¦The Virus⟧.
* Sticky Nickels are able to spawn as a result of killing enemies, effectively making them impossible to collect (aside from having an accompanying explosion to break it free after spawning, and being mindful enough to collect it in time), as it would have already disappeared by the time a bomb detonated to pick it up. ⟦i:137¦Remote Detonator⟧ would help, but it could end up in self-damage as the explosion would have to be extremely quick.
** Coin drops from enemies are generated when a room is first generated. If an enemy that begins in the room drops a nickel, dime, or penny variant, it will drop the same coin if you leave and re-enter the room. This makes items such as ⟦i:590¦Mercurius⟧, ⟦i:396¦Ventricle Razor⟧ and ⟦t:124¦Door Stop⟧ much more useful, as they allow the player to easily leave and re-enter the desired room, allowing the player to easily generate money to fuel the run. This will, however, make the enemies start dropping less and less money each time you kill them, eventually not dropping anything.
* In Co-Op, all players will need to use money to purchase items if Tainted Keeper is in the game, but enemies will also drop money regardless of who killed them.
** With this in mind, having the ⟦t:131¦Blessed Penny⟧ can earn a huge amount of Soul Hearts for the players who can use them quickly.
** Only the first item in a Boss Room needs to be purchased, the ones that spawn after it are free.
** This can be used to get Devil Deal items without losing health for all players.
* Tainted Keeper can utilize Sacrifice Rooms much more reliably and efficiently than other characters, because monsters reliably generate health. This can be done by leaving regular coin drops on the floor to go pick up, or alternating stepping on the sacrifice spikes with clearing a monster room. The latter is reliable to produce coins but risky because you're always entering an unknown monster room with one health, but can be used with restarts to start a run with one or two angel room items. Keep in mind that Tainted Keeper has to pay for items in Angel Rooms that you may get at the 6th sacrifice, though the item drop you may get at the 7th sacrifice will be free.
* Golden Pennies are able to spawn as a result of killing enemies. It still despawns like a normal coin unless picked up, in which case, any subsequent spawns will not disappear.
* Pressing reward plates is more worthwhile as enemies spawned by buttons reward extra coins.
* After entering Curse Rooms, try to exit the room immediately.
** If there are enemies in the room, you will not be able to leave, but the dropped coins will ensure you have health to exit safely.
** If there are no enemies, you'll exit the room while invincibility frames are active and will not lose your second coin heart.
** It is also recommended to save teleport cards/pills/items for entering curse rooms, so you may safely leave regardless.
* ⟨16⟩ Using the White Fire Place to turn into a ghostly form makes Boss Room items free of charge.

characters.strategy:
* The randomness of ⟦c:apollyon¦Apollyon⟧'s ⟦i:477¦Void⟧ is substituted for a guaranteed DPS upgrade with ⟦i:706¦Abyss⟧. This allows for easier judgement over whether active or mediocre items should be destroyed.
** Some Items give ⟦i:706¦Special locusts⟧. However, many of these Items are quite powerful, and may be more valuable if collected than if they are turned into Locusts.
* If Tainted Apollyon uses Abyss while picking up an active item, it will be turned into a locust; this is due to the change to items being able to be destroyed while being picked up in Repentance.
** This does not apply to any other characters, as Tainted Apollyon is the only one who can have Abyss in his consumable slot, and therefore both pick up an active item and use Abyss simultaneously.
** Be careful of swapping active items while picking up a new one as the old item will also be turned into a locust.
* In rooms where the player is presented a choice between several items (i.e. Boss Rush, Treasure Rooms on the alternate path, Treasure Rooms / Boss Rooms under the effect of ⟦i:414¦More Options⟧ / ⟦i:249¦There's Options⟧, certain Angel Room layouts, etc.) using Abyss will only give one locust for each item choice/set.
** This does not apply to rooms where the player can collect multiple items without penalty such as a Library, which can be fully absorbed, making them extremely useful to find.
* Locusts deal full damage per tick, meaning that it is important to find a balance between the number of locusts spawned and amount of damage dealt. Items from the Boss item pool are usually good sources of damage, so it may be worth it to seek them out immediately.
** ⟦i:149¦Ipecac⟧, for example, generates a unique poison locust with increased damage when Abyss consumes it; however, taking the item itself is almost always a superior choice, as the damage bonus from Ipecac affects all locusts Apollyon has, scaling further than the single locust would.
*** Already having very high damage and low tears, such as through ⟦i:169¦Polyphemus⟧, can make it a better idea to turn it into a locust, however.
* Like ⟦i:477¦Void⟧, Abyss can be used while holding an item, meaning it is completely possible to buy shop items and consume the item to grant a locust. One-time or low-use items such as ⟦i:195¦Mom's Coin Purse⟧ and ⟦i:603¦Battery Pack⟧ can be great items to do this with, assuming Pills and Batteries aren't the priority.
** This can also be used with blind item pedestals (such as on the alternate path or with Curse of the Blind), allowing Tainted Apollyon to use Abyss at the last second should he find the collected item to be undesirable.
* In Repentance Co-Op if Tainted Apollyon dies his red locusts will persist, following and attacking from his ghost.
* ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧: Locusts automatically aim at enemies, regardless of the direction Tainted Apollyon is firing in.
* Damage is especially important for Tainted Apollyon, as it helps both them and their locusts. Combined with the fact that Tears are much less important, items like ⟦i:169¦Polyphemus⟧ and ⟦i:310¦Eve's Mascara⟧ become even stronger than with most characters.
* ⟦t:125¦Extension Cord⟧: Every locust will generate a beam of electricity, significantly increasing the range and damage potential of Tainted Apollyon.
* ⟦i:422¦Glowing Hourglass⟧: Due to a bug, Glowing Hourglass can be used to duplicate locusts via Isaac teleporting to the previous room with the Glowing Hourglass and then using it again.
* ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧: Effectively gives locusts homing, making them much easier to deal full damage with. Also makes focusing on dodging much easier.
** ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧ + Guppy: Each tick of damage dealt counts for the purposes of the Guppy transformation, generating a constant flow of blue flies.
** ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧ + Homing: Tainted Apollyon can aim in the general direction of the enemy and fully focus on dodging.
* ⟦i:248¦Hive Mind⟧ and ⟦i:247¦BFFS!⟧ both increase the damage of locusts by 25%, which is especially helpful later in the run.
** Note that they do not stack.
* ⟦i:550¦Broken Shovel 1⟧: Makes for a very easy Quality 4 locust, assuming you find another active item early on.
* Items like ⟦i:245¦20/20⟧, ⟦i:2¦The Inner Eye⟧, and ⟦i:153¦Mutant Spider⟧ produce multiple high-quality locusts, granting large damage increases.
** Taking them is usually much less viable, as Tears don't usually make up as much of Tainted Apollyon's Damage. This is especially true for ⟦i:245¦20/20⟧ due to its 0.8x damage multiplier.
* ⟦i:638¦Eraser⟧: Eraser locusts have a chance to erase enemies on kill, which can make the run much easier, especially if gained and taken advantage of early on.
* Items that give high Tears and lower Damage, especially ⟦i:561¦Almond Milk⟧ and ⟦i:330¦Soy Milk⟧, heavily reduce the damage of locusts, making them potentially run-ruining depending on how important they are to a build.
* Most Luck-based Tear effects aren't as important for Tainted Apollyon due to his lower need for Tears in general.
** Their locusts, however, usually inherit their effects, making them useful if Abyssed.

characters.notes:
* Speed, range, shot speed, tears, and damage will be reduced to 75% for any amount over their base value. Familiars and Orbitals also deal only 75% of their usual damage.
* For example, with 4.5 damage, it is 1 damage over the base 3.5, and the 1 damage gets reduced to 0.75, ending up with a total of 4.25 damage.
* Fire rate multipliers change what is considered to be the base value, so with ⟦i:330¦Soy Milk⟧, only tears-ups above 15.00 will be reduced.
** The only exception is ⟦i:600¦Eye Drops⟧, which gets a reduction to its 1.2x fire rate multiplier if it's above base.
* Direct fire rate modifiers like ⟦i:228¦Mom's Perfume⟧ do not get reduced.
* Her soft tears cap is 4.43 instead of the normal 5.00.
* Lemegeton has a 25% chance to pull from the current room's item pool when creating item wisps, and as such can be abused by Tainted Bethany to obtain large amounts of useful items by saving her blood charges until she enters a room such as Angel Room, Devil Room, Secret Room, Shop, Curse Room, or even a Planetarium.
* Blended Hearts will count as red hearts and only contribute towards the red heart charge meter.
** Blended Hearts will give Soul Hearts once Tainted Bethany gains 99 blood charges.
* Items created by Lemegeton don't count towards Transformations.
* Items that normally grant consumables on pickup will not do so if created by Lemegeton.
* ⟨16⟩ Rotten Hearts count as one blood charge each like Half Red Hearts.

characters.strategy:
Throughout the majority of a run, Tainted Jacob is harassed by Dark Esau with no intended way of permanently getting rid of him. Because of this, playing as Tainted Jacob requires the player to manage both the playable Jacob and his vengeful brother Esau.
* Using ⟦i:722¦Anima Sola⟧ is key to success for Tainted Jacob, as it can help prevent damage from Dark Esau or turn him into a powerful weapon against enemies.
* In the ⟦s:mines¦Mines⟧, Tainted Jacob can intentionally run into Dark Esau in order to abuse the mechanics of The Lost form (specifically Flight in an area which normally removes any previous sources of flight you may have attained) to quickly and easily acquire the ⟦i:627¦Knife Piece 2⟧ with a rapid and flight-assisted escape if you are attempting to reach the ⟦s:corpse¦Corpse⟧ to defeat ⟦e:mother¦Mother⟧.
** Typically, the escape path would become excessively difficult due to both ⟦e:mother-s-shadow¦Mother's Shadow⟧ and Dark Esau attempting to charge at you in intervals which are typically out of sync, making it very difficult to escape without taking damage or potentially dying.
** By remaining in The Lost form, this also allows you bypass the damage which would normally be required to enter the door in order to advance to ⟦s:mausoleum¦Mausoleum⟧ / ⟦s:gehenna¦Gehenna⟧.
** It is recommended to fully clear the floor first, as Tainted Jacob remains in The Lost form until the next floor is reached.
* While in his Lost form, Tainted Jacob can take Devil Deals in the same way as the Lost. At the end of each floor with a Devil Deal spawn, it is possible to intentionally have Dark Esau turn Tainted Jacob into The Lost form in order to receive free Devil Deals.
* Items and transformations that give you flight (, , , and ) to be able to more easily dodge Dark Esau in rooms with pits and rocks, and/or spectral tears (quicker room clears with obstacles plus can cheese obstacle mechanics with Dark Esau) can help quickly clear rooms and avoid the brother's attacks.
* ⟦t:145¦Perfection⟧ is not lost upon getting hit by Dark Esau.
* It can actually be quite risky to take ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧. Each Dark Esau can charge in a different direction than the other, which ultimately increases your chances of getting hit by one of them.
Dark Esau himself should be respected. Being touched a single time by Dark Esau has a high chance of leading to a run's end by putting Jacob in his fragile Lost state for the remainder of a floor.
* Dark Esau deals no contact damage to Jacob while chained down with Anima Sola.
* Dark Esau's touch effect can be avoided while shielded, invulnerable, or otherwise immune to damage (such as with ⟦i:313¦Holy Mantle⟧ or ⟦i:210¦Gnawed Leaf⟧).
* Dark Esau keeps a consistent distance from Jacob, and will only charge if he is within this distance. Dark Esau will never actually be able to touch Jacob unless he starts his charge animation, charges, or Jacob runs into him.
** As such, running from and maintaining enough distance from Dark Esau will prevent him from charging.
** In some cases such as being next to an obstacle, Dark Esau will stop moving within the prop and will be unable to charge until Jacob moves away from it.
** Dark Esau will only charge at Jacob once he enters his cardinal line of sight. Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he is positioned diagonally from him, even if Jacob is standing still.
* Dark Esau's position at all times is determined by his position relative to the general layout of the floor, meaning he persists in the same location even when Tainted Jacob moves through rooms. Entering a new room cancels Esau's charge if he was preparing one or frees him if he was bound by Anima Sola.
** Caution should be taken when moving between rooms where Dark Esau is near the doorway, as this may lead to a situation where Tainted Jacob immediately runs into Dark Esau.
** Teleporting a great distance or traveling quickly through rooms with the help of special items or a high speed stat makes it harder for Dark Esau to catch up to Jacob.
** If Dark Esau is in the process of traveling between rooms, it is possible to use Anima Sola to chain him outside of the current area Tainted Jacob is in.
* As Dark Esau takes time to respawn after entering a new floor, the first few seconds on every floor can be used to explore rooms freely.
* Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he eats a Paralysis Pill.
Considering the damage Dark Esau can deal to enemies and the fact that Anima Sola can be canceled early by using it a second time, Dark Esau can become a powerful, albeit dangerous weapon to use against enemies by positioning Tainted Jacob in ways that manipulate him into charging into enemies. This is further compounded, as his charge attack ignores Boss Armor.
* Anima Sola can be used in an empty room to instantly summon Dark Esau in order to use him advantageously.
** Dark Esau's charge is able to single-handedly kill most early bosses in one or two hits. He can also be held in place with Anima Sola to bait chasing enemies, as Jacob can stand behind Dark Esau and cause them to run into him.
* In ⟦s:greed-mode¦Greed Mode⟧, Anima Sola will always be charged at the beginning of a new wave. This can be taken advantage of by binding Dark Esau before a new wave begins and then letting him charge into a freshly spawned enemy group or a priority enemy like a champion. Since releasing Dark Esau manually does not consume the item charge, the item will still be available to restrict him again immediately afterwards.
* Dark Esau's charge will extinguish Fire Places.
* Dark Esau cannot damage friendly enemies.
* When Dark Esau charges while in fear, he charges away from Tainted Jacob.
* Dark Esau cannot affect other players and ignores them completely.
** ⟨15⟩ If multiple players are playing Tainted Jacob, then any Tainted Jacob who touches any Dark Esau will still be turned into a ghost or die. Tainted Jacob players will only be able to use Anima Sola on their own Dark Esau, and if one of the Tainted Jacobs is completely killed, both Dark Esaus will begin to target the one that is still living.
** ⟨15⟩ When Tainted Jacob completely dies and is turned into a small ghost baby as a Co-Op partner, Dark Esau will still follow the ghost of Tainted Jacob if no other Tainted Jacob players are in the match, allowing them to still use him as a high damage weapon to help their teammates.
** ⟨16⟩ Dark Esau will no longer deal damage to enemies or charge at the ghost of Tainted Jacob until he is revived.
* If Tainted Jacob was turned into his ghostly form by Dark Esau, then dying and being revived upon completion of the boss will have him revive as his ghostly form.
** ⟨15⟩ If Tainted Jacob is dead at the start of a floor, Dark Esau will still spawn, but will target one of the living players instead. Unless they are also playing Tainted Jacob, he will never hurt them outside his spawning animation.
** ⟨16⟩ If Tainted Jacob is dead at the end of a floor, he will respawn at the start of the next floor.
* Dark Esau is considered a boss.
** Like every other "boss", Dark Esau can be spawned with debug commands. However, if playing as someone other than Tainted Jacob, the player will be immune to his attacks.
*** ⟦c:jacob¦Jacob⟧, even in his normal non-tainted form, is an exception. When touched by Dark Esau, he will take damage, but will not turn into a ghost. ⟦c:jacob¦Esau⟧, like most characters, is still immune to Dark Esau.
* When the console command "restart 39" is loaded, the player will be spawned as a ghostly version of Tainted Jacob. The only differences is that Dark Esau never seems to spawn and that this version of Tainted Jacob has the health of ⟦c:the-lost¦The Lost⟧.

weaknesses: Dark Esau le poursuit en permanence
tips: Dark Esau blesse aussi les ennemis : attirez-le à travers eux.

characters.notes:
* Both characters always co-exist and depend on each other; Tainted Soul is incapable of firing tears or dealing damage in almost any manner, and likewise, Tainted Forgotten is incapable of moving on their own. Tainted Soul is able to pick up and move around with, or throw, Tainted Forgotten, similar to how one holds and throws ⟦i:42¦Bob's Rotten Head⟧. Otherwise, Tainted Forgotten has a melee bone weapon like ⟦c:the-forgotten¦The Forgotten⟧ does, which he can swing and throw while on the ground.
** Tainted Forgotten will swing his bone at the same time Tainted Soul throws him, and this swing will deal 3x the normal damage, and the impact itself will deal 5 damage.
* Tainted Forgotten is also completely invulnerable, and instead, Tainted Soul acts as his 'hitbox' and will take damage like any character. Both characters share the same pool of Soul Hearts (they cannot have Red Heart Containers), and if the last one is lost, they both die.
* Enemies almost always target Tainted Soul and ignore Tainted Forgotten, but the latter's body can be used to block enemy projectiles and movement.
* Both share the same pool of pickups, similar to ⟦c:the-forgotten¦The Forgotten⟧. Tainted Forgotten can pick up items and consumables when he's thrown at them, as well as open Chests or unlock doors.
* Tainted Forgotten can be thrown into a door to enter the next room (including Curse Rooms, which deal no damage to Tainted Forgotten), and after entering a room, Tainted Soul will always be holding him. With practice, they can very rapidly traverse the floor, spending a fraction of a second in any cleared room.
* When placing a Bomb, it will be placed underneath Tainted Forgotten, and the same is true when dropping trinkets or Cards, etc.
* Any items picked up will normally behave as if Tainted Forgotten picked them up and don't directly affect Tainted Soul; for example, orbital familiars will orbit Tainted Forgotten. Speed upgrades on the other hand will apply to Tainted Soul, among other examples. Effects that grant invincibility, i.e. ⟦i:58¦Book of Shadows⟧, will apply to Tainted Soul, whether or not there's visual indication of this.
* Tainted Soul can open the door to ⟦s:mausoleum¦Mausoleum⟧ / ⟦s:gehenna¦Gehenna⟧ without losing any health while not holding Tainted Forgotten.
* If Tainted Soul picks up Tainted Forgotten while the latter is charging a bone toss, it will throw it once the player releases the attack button.
* If Tainted Forgotten's range reaches high enough numbers, his melee bone swing will occur away from him, which can result in an inability to deal damage to enemies too close to him.
* Bulbs will never attack both Tainted Forgotten or Tainted Soul.
characters.strategy:
* In order to one-throw-kill as many enemies as possible, Tainted Forgotten's build should focus on Damage. Having high Speed is also important, as it allows Tainted Soul to pick Tainted Forgotten up easier. Tears and Range are less useful than normal for Tainted Forgotten.
* Items that enhance melee attack radius (such as size-up items, ⟦i:69¦Chocolate Milk⟧, ⟦i:153¦Mutant Spider⟧, ⟦i:68¦Technology⟧) are also recommended. Items that split tears on hit like ⟦i:531¦Haemolacria⟧ are beneficial as well.
* Items with area of effect damage such as ⟦i:574¦Monstrance⟧ and ⟦i:559¦120 Volt⟧ apply their effect to Tainted Forgotten, making them incredibly powerful for large crowds and stationary bosses.
* Care should be taken when fighting enemies spawned in Devil Rooms, Shops and Black Markets, as Tainted Forgotten will buy anything he's thrown into if possible, with potentially fatal results.
* Some pills don't work or are irrelevant because they apply their effects to Tainted Forgotten. Paralysis is one example.
* Be careful of Mom's Hands, because they can grab Tainted Forgotten. This will deal no damage, but will still teleport Tainted Forgotten back to the starting room.
* Tainted Soul can open Mimic Chests without taking damage.
* Tainted Soul can activate the stop button in ⟦s:greed-mode¦Greed Mode⟧ without taking damage, at the price of one less coin spawning in the next wave's reward. Tainted Forgotten's body can also be used to activate the button, which does not cost a coin.
* Tainted Soul can pass through the mirror in ⟦s:downpour¦Downpour⟧ / ⟦s:dross¦Dross⟧ II without touching the White Fire Place (in fact, nothing happens when he flies over it), and will keep his life bar, which makes the trek considerably safer.
** If Tainted Forgotten is thrown into the White Fire Place, he transforms into ⟦c:the-lost¦The Lost⟧ (though he is still invulnerable); Tainted Soul will have ⟦i:313¦Holy Mantle⟧ protection (if unlocked), but will die if damage is taken after it's broken like normal.
* Items that inflict Fear like ⟦i:228¦Mom's Perfume⟧ and ⟦i:554¦2Spooky⟧ should be avoided because enemies will flee from Tainted Forgotten instead of Tainted Soul, making it harder to hit enemies while also offering Tainted Soul little protection.
* Charmed enemies may pursue Tainted Forgotten instead of other enemies, which can be ideal for bringing and keeping them within range of his melee attack.
* Tear effects from items such as ⟦i:496¦Euthanasia⟧ and ⟦i:463¦Sulfuric Acid⟧ will activate on both body throws and melee attacks.
* All contact damage attacks such as ⟦i:300¦Aries⟧ and ⟦i:13¦The Virus⟧ are tripled in strength and will apply when throwing Tainted Forgotten. The damage is added on top of the normal 5 points his body impact does. Tainted Soul however does not benefit from them at all.

strengths: The Soul vole et peut lancer The Forgotten comme une arme
weaknesses: Contrôle très inhabituel, The Soul est fragile
tips: Entraînez-vous au lancer : c'est la principale source de dégâts.
