characters.notes:
* Just as the Holy Mantle effect from the Holy Card negates damage taken in the first place, items such as ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧, ⟦t:23¦Missing Poster⟧ and ⟦p:soul-of-lazarus¦Soul of Lazarus⟧ will revive Tainted Lost after death. This means that items that normally take effect upon taking damage will affect Tainted Lost upon death and revival.
* Beating Delirium with ⟦c:the-lost¦The Lost⟧ is not required for Tainted Lost to obtain the ⟦p:holy-card¦Holy Card⟧, or for Holy Cards to spawn during the run.
* As with The Lost, Devil Room items and Black Market items can be taken for free, but will be presented as a choice. Taking one item as a deal will cause the others in the room to disappear.
characters.strategy:
With only a single ⟦p:holy-card¦Holy Card⟧ for defense, defensive items become just as important as offensive ones, as taking more than a single hit in the entire run may prove fatal. However, because all items not marked as "offensive" will automatically be rerolled, defensive options available are less plentiful.
* A good way to secure a powerful run is to visit as many Boss Challenge Rooms as possible. It is possible for the player to use the alternate floors to their advantage by sticking to the second floor of each chapter. By visiting ⟦s:downpour¦Downpour⟧ II / ⟦s:dross¦Dross⟧ II, the player can also get an extra boss item from the Mirrored World. This strategy comes with the added risk of having to fight more bosses, but provides the potential to snowball the player's stats and make later floors much easier to survive in.
* Be careful of any Chests, which could be a Mimic Chest or a Haunted Chest.
* Skulls can be a source of finding cards which in turn can be a ⟦p:holy-card¦Holy Card⟧.
* Waiting before using the ⟦p:holy-card¦Holy Card⟧ until after the Shop has been found in case a ⟦i:286¦Blank Card⟧ is available for sale can prove helpful.
* Be wary of taking items that automatically attack enemies in case they kill exploding enemies nearby. This includes items like ⟦i:559¦120 Volt⟧, ⟦i:113¦Demon Baby⟧, and items that spawn blue flies.

tips: Considéré comme l'un des personnages les plus difficiles : progressez lentement et gardez vos cartes de protection.

completionMarks.description: Vaincre Mom's Heart (It Lives! après 11 victoires) à la fin du Womb, de l'Utero ou du Scarred Womb.
Vaincre Isaac à la fin de la Cathedral.
Vaincre Satan à la fin du Sheol.
Vaincre ??? (Blue Baby) dans le Chest — The Polaroid est nécessaire pour y entrer depuis la Cathedral.
Vaincre The Lamb dans la Dark Room — The Negative facilite grandement l'accès depuis le Sheol.
Terminer le Boss Rush (porte ouverte si Mom est vaincue en moins de 20 minutes).
Vaincre Hush dans le Blue Womb (porte ouverte si Mom's Heart est vaincu en moins de 30 minutes).
Vaincre Mega Satan derrière la porte dorée du Chest ou de la Dark Room (Key Piece 1 + 2 ou clé dorée équivalente).
Vaincre Delirium au cœur de The Void.
Vaincre Mother à la fin du Corpse (chemin alternatif Downpour/Dross → Mines/Ashpit → Mausoleum/Gehenna).
Vaincre Dogma puis The Beast dans Home, au terme de l'Ascension.
Vaincre Ultra Greed en mode Greed ; la version « difficile » de cette marque correspond au mode Greedier (depuis Afterbirth+).

synergies.text:
if Metronome is used while the shield is active, any stat changes or familiars/orbitals generated from Metronome will persist between rooms until Metronome is used again or replaced with another active item. Items that modify your stats and have other additional effects will keep the stats but the effect will be gone after leaving the room. For example, the tears down applied from ⟦i:2¦The Inner Eye⟧ will persist between rooms, but Isaac will not shoot three tears at once.
* Some items behave unusually after leaving the room while the Holy Mantle shield was active:
** Items that grant flight: Isaac's appearance is reset back to normal, but he is still able to fly.
** ⟦i:11¦1up!⟧: the mushroom familiar continues to follow Isaac, but doesn't grant an extra life.
** ⟦i:48¦Cupid's Arrow⟧: the tear appearance is reset back to normal, but the tears still travel through enemies.
** ⟦i:257¦Fire Mind⟧: the tear appearance is reset back to normal, but tears can still explode when they hit an enemy.
** ⟦i:317¦Mysterious Liquid⟧: the tear appearance is reset back to normal, but tears will still leave green creep on the ground.

synergies.text:
The laser becomes dark purple and automatically fires at a controllable crosshair. The crosshair behaves nearly identically to the one created by ⟦i:394¦Marked⟧ (including in its synergies and interactions with other items), but the laser itself always fires in the cardinal directions and bends toward the crosshair rather than directly targeting it.
* ⟦c:azazel¦Azazel⟧: Like Brimstone, except that his short beam becomes a lasso. The loop starts where the beam would normally end and extends out to the cross-hair.
* Brimstone/Technology + ⟦i:69¦Chocolate Milk⟧: The closer the crosshair is to Isaac, the less charged the laser will be, and vice versa.
* Brimstone/Technology + ⟦i:360¦Incubus⟧/⟦i:698¦Twisted Pair⟧: The familiars fire a straight laser towards the crosshair.
* Brimstone/Technology + ⟦i:394¦Marked⟧/⟦i:465¦Analog Stick⟧: The laser more closely follows the crosshair's position relative to Isaac. In Brimstone's case, moving the crosshair while the laser is firing makes the laser bend toward it rather than changing the firing angle of the laser itself.
* Brimstone/Technology + ⟦i:680¦Montezuma's Revenge⟧: The brown beam has a similar interaction as ⟦c:azazel¦Azazel⟧'s beam but cannot create the crosshair on its own. Corn shots are unaffected.
* Brimstone/Technology + ⟦i:643¦Revelation⟧/⟦i:244¦Tech.5⟧/⟦i:152¦Technology 2⟧: The Revelation, Tech.5, and Technology 2 lasers are also affected by the crosshair but cannot create the crosshair on their own.

* This makes for a great synergy since the fetuses are homing and stay up much longer than regular tears.

synergies.text:
The fetuses drop small bombs when they touch an enemy. The bomb's damage follows Dr. Fetus' damage calculation, based on half of the fetuses damage. A fetus can drop only one bomb.
* The fetuses' bombs do not benefit from Isaac's bomb effects such as ⟦i:256¦Hot Bombs⟧ or ⟦i:125¦Bobby-Bomb⟧. However, they do benefit from Isaac's tear effects and have the appearance of the corresponding bombs. For example, ⟦i:256¦Hot Bombs⟧ from ⟦i:257¦Fire Mind⟧, ⟦i:125¦Bobby-Bomb⟧ from homing tears. As such, ⟦i:224¦Cricket's Body⟧, ⟦i:104¦The Parasite⟧, and ⟦i:169¦Polyphemus⟧ leave a subsequent bomb or bombs, and ⟦i:317¦Mysterious Liquid⟧ leaves a creep.
* Dr. Fetus + ⟦i:149¦Ipecac⟧: The fetuses explode before dropping any bomb.
* Dr. Fetus + ⟦i:531¦Haemolacria⟧: Fetuses will both drop a bomb on touching an enemy and burst into multiple small bombs upon hitting the ground.

synergies.text:
Some Fetuses stick to enemies, expand, then explode. However, they do not inflict their contact damage while sticking.
* Explosivo + ⟦i:114¦Mom's Knife⟧: The knives from fetuses with Explosivo's effect create exploding tears for each damaging tick. The explosions from a knife deal 60 + half of the fetus' damage which held it.
* Explosivo + ⟦i:704¦Berserk!⟧ / ⟦i:579¦Spirit Sword⟧ / ⟦c:the-forgotten¦The Forgotten⟧ / ⟦c:tainted-forgotten¦Tainted Forgotten⟧: The clubs/swords from fetuses with Explosivo's effect create exploding tears for each damaged enemy from their attack. The explosions from a club/sword deal 60 + the damage its attack dealt.
* Explosivo + ⟦i:68¦Technology⟧: The lasers from fetuses with Explosivo's effect create exploding tears for each damaged enemy from their attack. The tears inherit the fetuses' property, including laser attacks, from which can create more tears. The tears from a laser deal 60 + the laser's damage they originated, and their lasers deal the same as the lasers they originated. Fetuses can fire lasers while sticking to an enemy and spin, while tears do not spin.
* Explosivo + ⟦i:395¦Tech X⟧: The laser rings from fetuses with Explosivo's effect create exploding tears for each damaging tick. The explosions from a ring deal 60 + the ring's damage.

The fetuses from the burst also hold clubs/swords which are able to create another wave of spores. The damage of attacks are calculated based on half of the spores' flat 3.5 damage.
** ⟦i:704¦Berserk!⟧ / ⟦c:the-forgotten¦The Forgotten⟧: Their swings deal 10.5 damage.
** ⟦c:tainted-forgotten¦Tainted Forgotten⟧: Their swings deal 8.4 damage.
** ⟦i:579¦Spirit Sword⟧: Their swing attacks/spin attacks/projectiles deal 8.75/24/11 damage.
* Mucormycosis + ⟦i:68¦Technology⟧: The lasers from fetuses with Mucormycosis' effect create spores for each damaged enemy from their attack. The spores inherit the fetuses' property including laser attacks, which can create another spores. The fetuses from the burst also has laser attacks which are able to create another wave of spores. Their laser attacks deal 3.5 damage, based on the spores' flat 3.5 damage. Fetuses can fire lasers while sticking to an enemy and spin, while spores do not spin.
* Mucormycosis + ⟦i:395¦Tech X⟧: The laser rings from fetuses with Mucormycosis' effect create spores for each damaging tick. The fetuses from the burst are also surrounded by laser rings which are able to create another wave of spores. Their rings deal 1.75 damage, based on half of the spores' flat 3.5 damage.

bosses.behavior:
??? lies on the ground in the middle of the room and does not begin attacking until he takes damage.
During all three of ???'s phases, he performs similar attacks to Isaac, but at a faster pace. He also shoots multiple projectiles in the player's direction at fixed intervals. After taking enough damage, he begins to shoot double and triple projectiles.
* Each projectile has a chance of having a homing effect.
??? remains stationary on the ground and performs the following attacks:
* Shoots 7-8 rapid-fire lines of projectiles in all directions that expand outwards. After taking enough damage, these lines curve while travelling.
* Shoots 8 lines of 2 projectiles in all directions that expand outwards. Each line consists of one normal projectile and one homing projectile. After taking enough damage, these lines curve while travelling.
* After taking enough damage, ??? summons Attack Flies, Moters, or Pooters that orbit around himself.
** Pooters have a farther orbit than the other flies.
** Attack Flies spawned from Moters chase Isaac instead of orbiting ???.
2 Eternal Flies that can block tears begin to circle ???, who stands up but remains stationary and performs the following attacks:
* Continues to spawn orbiting flies.
* Fires 4 homing projectiles in a lop-sided X pattern.
* Fires 8 homing projectiles in all directions.
??? grows a pair of angelic wings and is no longer stationary, slowly drifting towards Isaac and performing the following attacks:
* Spawning orbiting eternal flies (with increasing frequency compared to the previous phase).
* Teleporting to a position in front of the player - predicting their movements and attempting to cut them off. ??? will teleport directly on top of the player if the player is stationary.
* Shooting 2 projectile patterns from the first phase.

bosses.behavior:
Baby Plum floats slowly towards Isaac and attempts to orbit a certain distance around him. She will not break this distance unless she performs an attack with a movement ability. While chasing Isaac, she also performs the following attacks:
* Spits a diagonal stream of projectiles, propelling herself backwards across the room and bouncing off any walls she collides into.
** Randomly scattered in the stream are larger projectiles that deal a whole heart of damage.
** Baby Plum takes increased knockback from any source during this attack.
* Twirls towards Isaac, sending out a spiral of projectiles.
** The spiral will always start pointing down, then make a full rotation starting in the direction closest to Isaac.
* Slams the ground, firing two rings of projectiles outwards and leaving behind a small pool of Red Creep. The inner ring consists of 14 slow-moving projectiles while the outer one consists of 8 fast-moving projectiles.
** The outer ring's projectiles will always be fired in the cardinal and ordinal directions, while the inner ring's projectiles will have a random spread.
* Upon death, releases a ring of 10 projectiles.
If Baby Plum doesn't take damage for 30 seconds, she will wave at the screen before flying away. The Boss Room item that spawns when the room is cleared will also be replaced by ⟦i:650¦Plum Flute⟧ if Isaac isn't already holding it.
* If Baby Plum takes damage, it does not negate the ability to spare her but rather resets the timer for her to fly away.
* This does not apply in Greed mode, or any rooms she appears in that are not actually her own boss room.
bosses.notes: * The copy of Baby Plum created by ⟦i:697¦Vanishing Twin⟧ drops a random boss item if spared.

bosses.behavior:
Big Horn alternates between attacking with his arms and his head.
Big Horn spawns 2 or 3 small holes; one of his arms has a chance of appearing from each hole. Each arm can perform the following attacks either by itself or in conjunction with another arm:
* Throws a Troll Bomb towards Isaac.
* Throws 3 Troll Bombs in a spread towards Isaac.
** Every Troll Bomb has a chance of being a ⟦i:256¦Hot Bombs⟧ Bomb or a Mega Troll Bomb.
** ⟨24⟩ If the area is Flooded, instead of Hot Bombs, he will send out ⟦i:220¦Sad Bombs⟧.
* If Big Horn tosses a bomb into one of the empty holes, Big Horn’s hand appears out of that hole and tosses out the same type of bomb.
* Quickly slaps the ground 3 times with an empty hand while traveling towards Isaac.
** This attack can kill any Dark Balls it touches.
* ⟨7⟩ If a hole is empty, there is an extremely rare chance to spawn a low-health version of ⟦e:little-horn¦Little Horn⟧.
* ⟨24⟩ Holds up a Little Horn in his palm which spits out 3 small homing Dark Balls in quick succession.
** If Big Horn dies while performing this attack, Little Horn hops off the hand and continues the fight, but with low health.
Big Horn's head can perform the following attacks after appearing from a large hole:
* Spits out a large Dark Ball beneath him that homes in on Isaac.
* Spits out two large Dark Balls beneath him that travel diagonally, bouncing when colliding with walls or Isaac's tears. These do not home.
* Occasionally spits out 3 Dark Balls; 2 homing and 1 non-homing.
** ⟨7⟩ The Dark Balls can hit and damage Big Horn, destroying themselves in the process.
* After spawning a Dark Ball, there is a very small window where Bombs can be kicked into his mouth. If fed a Bomb, Big Horn is temporarily stunned, and plays a unique animation, during which he takes 20% more damage.
** ⟨24⟩ Additionally, the Bomb also explodes in his mouth, dealing considerable damage.
* Big Horn's head occasionally pauses and returns into the hole without attacking.
** This always occurs at the start of the battle.
bosses.notes: * The Hot Bombs (⟨24⟩ and Sad Bombs) he throws are not affected by ⟦t:63¦Safety Scissors⟧.

source.source: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki (wiki.gg) — CC BY-SA 4.0

bosses.behavior:
Makes hops towards Isaac and can perform the following attacks:
* If Isaac is close it, hops in place and upon landing:
** ⟨7⟩ Shoots 8 projectiles in all directions.
** ⟨24⟩ Sends out a burst of large disorganized projectiles in all directions.
* If Isaac is far away it, leaps off-screen and lands on Isaac's position; upon landing:
** ⟨7⟩ Shoots 12 small projectiles in all directions.
** ⟨24⟩ Shoots 8 larger projectiles in all directions.
* Once enough health is depleted, it splits into two medium versions of itself that continue to hop after Isaac. Medium Blastocysts only hop after Isaac if he is within a certain distance from them. Otherwise, they hop around randomly.
** Each medium form shoots 6 projectiles in all directions by hopping in place. The orientation of the projectiles depends on Isaac's position.
* Once enough health is depleted, each medium Blastocyst splits into two small versions. Small Blastocysts no longer hop after Isaac and only hop around randomly.
** Each small form shoots 4 projectiles in the cardinal directions after pausing for a moment.
* Each of these small Blastocysts leaves an Embryo behind upon defeat.
Blastocyst's large and medium forms deal a whole heart of contact damage.
bosses.notes:
* Blastocyst can be encountered in groups consisting of:
** 1 large Blastocyst and 2 small Blastocysts.
** 1 large Blastocyst and 6 Embryos.
** 2 medium Blastocysts and 2 small Blastocysts.
* The medium and small Blastocysts' projectiles deal full heart damage regardless of chapter.

bosses.behavior:
Blighted Ovum starts separated into two parts.
* Suture, now a ghost, is invincible and slowly floats towards Isaac, firing a horizontal ⟦i:118¦Brimstone⟧ shot whenever Isaac is to his left or right. Suture cannot be killed and will die once Contusion does.
* Contusion constantly chases Isaac while leaving behind a trail of Red Creep, and he periodically charges and gains speed. Unlike ⟦e:gemini¦Gemini⟧, he will not stop for a breath but slows down to his regular speed.
bosses.notes:
* ⟨4⟩ Suture can be killed by ⟦i:503¦Little Horn⟧.
* If encountered in a Double Trouble boss fight, Suture's ⟦i:118¦Brimstone⟧ laser can damage the other boss.

bosses.behavior:
Brownie remains stationary and performs the following attacks:
* Each time Brownie takes enough damage, he spawns a single Brownie Corn; if Brownie takes a lot of damage in a single instance, the Brownie Corns are spawned together in a group.
* Occasionally spawns a group 5-8 Brownie Corns upon taking damage.
** While moving during some attacks, he crushes any Brownie Corns in his path, regaining 3 HP for each.
* Farts, pushing away Isaac and knocking back any Brownie Corns if they are too close.
* Spins a short distance across the room, bouncing off walls and finishing with a fart.
** Sometimes leaves slippery brown creep and a Corn Mine in his path.
* Slides across the room, bouncing off walls, while leaving a trail of slippery Brown Creep, continuously spawning Corn Mines, and occasionally shooting corny projectiles towards Isaac. Finishes this attack with a fart.
** The Corn Mines' corn projectiles and gas can damage and poison Brownie. While poisoned, he leaves damaging green creep instead of Brown Creep.
* Twirls and jumps 4-6 times around the room, creating a puddle of Brown Creep every time he lands and tossing corny projectiles in random directions.
** Brownie can sometimes directly chain into this attack from his spinning and sliding attacks instead of finishing them with farts.
Brownie's expression when idle changes as he gets damaged by Isaac – going from happy to grumpy. This appears to have a correlation with how aggressive he is in performing attacks, chaining attacks, and how many corny projectiles are released in his attacks.
* When Brownie reaches around 25% health, he degrades into a 75 HP ⟦e:dangle¦Dangle⟧ that behaves regularly.
bosses.notes:
* Brownie may be paired along with regular Dips in a Boss Room.
* If a ⟦i:209¦Butt Bombs⟧ Bomb goes off in the same room as Brownie, it heals him.
** ⟨28⟩ Butt Bombs effect on ⟦i:52¦Dr. Fetus⟧ or ⟦i:168¦Epic Fetus⟧ does not heal Brownie.
** ⟨24⟩ The skeleton version of ⟦c:tainted-forgotten¦Tainted Forgotten⟧ in the Hot Potato challenge does heal Brownie. Thus, butt bombs should be skipped to avoid a potential softlock.
* ⟦i:291¦Flush!⟧ kills Brownie instantly and causes him to leave behind 6 Brownie Corns.
* If Brownie is inflicted by any status effect, he leaves a creep with that same effect (e.g. ⟦i:89¦Spider Bite⟧ gives him white creep if he's affected).

bosses.behavior:
Bumbino slowly moves towards Isaac and can perform the following attacks:
* Swipes forward to clear a path to Isaac if Bumbino is obstructed by obstacles while chasing him.
* Performs two swipes, one in Isaac's direction, followed by another swipe in the opposite direction; these swipes can break obstacles. Then slams the ground, releasing 8 rock projectiles in all directions as well as 4 rock waves diagonally.
** If Bumbino hits a wall or a pit with a swipe he is momentarily stunned, interrupting this attack and causing rock projectiles to fall from the ceiling.
** His swipe attack will also deflect incoming projectiles.
* Charges in Isaac's direction when vertically aligned with him and a wall, breaking all obstacles caught in his path. Bumbino will become stunned upon impacting the wall, launching a cluster of rock projectiles in the opposite direction and causes rock projectiles to fall from the ceiling.
** If Isaac is close to the impact, he is pushed away.
* Launches a ⟦i:209¦Butt Bombs⟧ Bomb in Isaac's direction.
All of Bumbino's attacks deal 1 Heart of damage.
Additionally, Bumbino attempts to pick up any dropped Coins, similar to ⟦e:ultra-greed¦Ultra Greed⟧, but without the healing.
* He prioritizes picking up coins on the ground over attacking.
* He cannot pick up Sticky Nickels, but will try indefinitely if one should spawn in the room, effectively anchoring him to one spot.
* Getting hit by Bumbino's swipes may sometimes cause Isaac to drop coins.
* If Bumbino picks up at least 12 cents worth of coins, he drops an extra item from the following list and then leaves the room:
bosses.notes: * Bumbino cannot spawn copies of items that Isaac has already encountered/collected. Once Bumbino's item pool is exhausted, he will only drop ⟦i:36¦The Poop⟧.

bosses.behavior:
C.H.A.D. moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:
* C.H.A.D. charges at Isaac whenever he lines up with one of his cardinal directions.
** Like ⟦e:chub¦Chub⟧, C.H.A.D. eats any Bombs dropped in his path; stunning him for a moment before dealing considerable damage.
* Spawns 1-2 Suckers.
* As he gets damaged, C.H.A.D. gradually shrinks in size and increases in speed and attack frequency.
bosses.notes:
* ⟨24⟩ C.H.A.D is much less common than his counterpart, spawning only 1/4th as often.
* C.H.A.D can spawn alongside 2 Boils or 2 Red Boom Flies.
* Each segment of C.H.A.D. can be individually damaged, so a single piercing tear could hit C.H.A.D. multiple times.
** ⟨24⟩ Piercing shots no longer damage segmented enemies multiple times per attack.

bosses.behavior:
Carrion Queen is only vulnerable in the flesh segment of her behind. She moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:
* Carrion Queen charges at Isaac whenever he lines up with one of her cardinal directions.
** Like ⟦e:chub¦Chub⟧, Carrion Queen eats any Bombs dropped in her path; stunning her for a moment before dealing considerable damage.
* Spawns a damaging Red Poop, up to a maximum of 5.
** She damages and destroys Red Poop she charges into.
* When below half health, Carrion Queen begins to move diagonally, similar to ⟦e:the-hollow¦The Hollow⟧, but without flight. She no longer performs her previous attacks from Phase 1.
** She will bounce off of obstacles and her own Red Poop damaging it and destroying it in the process.
Carrion Queen deals a whole heart of contact damage in both phases.
bosses.notes: * Piercing tears make the fight much easier, as tears can pass through Carrion Queen's invulnerable segments and hit her vulnerable segment.

bosses.behavior:
Chimera trots quickly in Isaac's direction, slowly building up speed. When fast enough, it leaves a trail of harmful green creep and makes wide turns due to its momentum. It can also perform the following attacks:
* Spits out 5 Small Maggots.
** Any Small Maggots it walks into are killed.
** Unlike its other attacks, Chimera can perform this one without interrupting its chase and its built up speed.
* Spits out a Sick Boom Fly and throws it towards Isaac.
* Jumps twice towards Isaac, shooting out a radius of 8 tears on the first landing and 4 rock waves in diagonal directions on the second landing.
* Shoots out 8 ⟦i:149¦Ipecac⟧ shots towards where Isaac is predicted to move. The landing position of each projectile is marked on the ground.
Once its HP has dropped to about half, it makes a final charge towards Isaac before tripping and dividing the head and body into separate entities. It will take increasingly reduced damage as it approaches 50% HP until it transitions phases.
* The head continuously makes leaps towards Isaac and slides a distance after landing while leaving a trail of damaging red creep. It can also perform the following attacks:
** Shoots out 4 spreads of 5 projectiles in Isaac's direction.
** Performs three quick dashes, similar to ⟦e:dingle¦Dingle⟧, leaving Red Creep. The first 2 dashes are towards Isaac while the final dash is towards its body. After completing the final dash the body can pick the head up and throw it at Isaac, leaving a trail of projectiles as it travels and creating a burst of projectiles where the head collides with a wall.
*** If the body is performing another attack during the head's charges, the head will charge at Isaac for its third charge instead.
** If the body dies before the head, it continuously makes long charges at Isaac, bouncing off any walls while also leaving Red Creep.
* The body continues to chase Isaac like the first phase but at a slower pace. It can also perform the following attacks:
** Fires a green-hued ⟦i:118¦Brimstone⟧ beam downwards if Isaac is directly above or below it. It is propelled upwards by this beam until it hits the wall.
** Runs quickly towards Isaac building momentum before leaping and rolling around the room bouncing off walls, similar to ⟦e:the-cage¦The Cage⟧.
** If the head dies before the body, the body continuously rolls around like The Cage for the rest of the battle.

bosses.behavior:
Chub moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:
* Charges at Isaac whenever she lines up with one of her cardinal directions.
** Chub eats any Bombs dropped in her path; stunning her for a moment before dealing considerable damage.
* Spawns 1-2 Chargers, up to a maximum of 5 (occasionally 6 if she spawns 2 while there are 4 alive).
** Chub's charge attack can damage and kill any Chargers.
Chub deals a whole heart of contact damage.
bosses.notes:
* Chub is often paired with Chargers in the boss room.
** ⟨30⟩ She can also be paired with Drowned Chargers.
* When using ⟦i:52¦Dr. Fetus⟧' bomb combined with a shot type that passes through enemies, Chub will not eat the bomb.
* Each segment of Chub can be individually damaged, so a single piercing tear could hit Chub multiple times.
** ⟨24⟩ Piercing shots no longer damage segmented enemies multiple times per attack.
* Chub will eat Troll Bombs (such as those set by other bosses) just like bombs dropped by Isaac.
* ⟦i:136¦Best Friend⟧ can damage Chub if eaten, similar to a bomb.
* ⟦i:631¦Meat Cleaver⟧ can instantly kill Chub.
* Chub can spawn without the last segment.

bosses.behavior:
Clog remains stationary in the center of the room, with the exception of a rare boss room layout where he spawns at the top center. He performs the following attacks:
* Spits out a Drip below him, repeating this attack a random number of times.
** Clog stops spitting out Drips if 4 are already alive.
** Clog alternates between spitting out Drips and performing his other attacks. If 4 Drips are alive, he skips spawning them and continuously uses his other attacks.
* Creates three lines of farts that spread across the room, knocking away Isaac and Drips. Each fart has a chance to spawn Poops.
** 1-2 Corny Poops are spawned in this attack, and no more than 3 can be up at a time.
* Shoots out 4 spiraling lines of projectiles, consisting of either slow projectiles with small gaps in between or fast projectiles with large gaps in between.
** The projectiles pass over poop for 1 second after being fired, and are blocked by poop afterward.
** The gaps between the slower projectiles are barely large enough for Isaac to move between them if he is next to the left or right wall.
* Clog spins and causes the water in the room to circulate around him clockwise or counterclockwise, catching Isaac and any Drips, Bombs, and/or Pickups in its current.
** This attack can only be used if at least 2 Drips are alive.
** Like other water-based effects in the ⟦s:dross¦Dross⟧ floor, Isaac is unaffected by this current if he has flight.
* Upon Clog's defeat, he and all remaining Drips are "flushed" away identical to the effect of using ⟦i:291¦Flush!⟧ on them.
bosses.notes:
* If a ⟦i:209¦Butt Bombs⟧ Bomb goes off in the same room as Clog, it heals him.
* The hitbox of poops is small enough for Isaac and the Drips spawned by Clog to move diagonally between them, even if they are undamaged.
** This happens frequently when Clog causes the water to circulate and forces them to be pressed against the poops he spawns.
* All poops created by Clog are significantly less likely to spawn pickups until Clog is defeated and Isaac re-enters the room, at which point they return to having their normal pickup drop chance.
* ⟦i:291¦Flush!⟧ kills Clog instantly and causes him to leave behind 6 Dips.

source.source: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki (wiki.gg) — CC BY-SA 4.0

bosses.behavior:
Clutch always spawns alongside 3 Clickety Clacks that it utilizes in its attacks. Phase 1 uses the following pattern:
* Randomly possesses one of the three Clickety Clacks, causing its head to spin and shoot 8 bone shots in the cardinal and ordinal directions. While possessing a Clickety Clack, Clutch is immune to all damage.
** Clutch will swap between Clickety Clacks at random intervals, or when the Clickety Clack he is possessing is killed. It can be briefly damaged when it is flying between Clickety Clacks.
** The possessed Clickety Clack will pursue Isaac and fire chains of bone projectiles at him when lined up in a cardinal direction, similar to a Bony, but will also move along a cardinal axis to stay in line with Isaac' position while shooting.
** The other non-possessed Clickety Clacks will be shielded, akin to the shield from a Bishop.
* When a Clickety Clack is killed, the bone pile it leaves behind will not regenerate. Instead, it will spawn a small purple fire that occasionally summons a bone projectile on its position before shooting it at Isaac, similarly to a Necro.
* When all three Clickety Clacks are killed, Clutch will be forcefully ejected and stunned, making it open to attack.
** After enough damage is dealt, Clutch will scream and revive all three Clickety Clacks, restarting the process.
Phase 2 begins once Clutch reaches 25% health. Clutch will scream, destroy all of the Clickety Clacks, and spawn bone orbitals that orbit Clutch and block tears.
* The bone orbitals follow Clutch loosely, dragging behind its movements.
* Indestructible purple fires will be left in the wake of the dead Clickety Clacks.
In this phase, Clutch will only perform the following attack:
* Rushes to Isaac's position in the room, stops, and shoots six volleys of six purple flames, in an alternating pattern.
** Clutch repeats this attack until its health is depleted.
* Upon death, Clutch creates a large explosion that deals 4 ticks of 80 damage to all monsters.
bosses.notes:
* If ⟦i:638¦Eraser⟧ is used on Clickety Clacks prior to entering the boss room, the boss fight will begin directly in the second phase.
* If all the Clickety Clack bone piles are destroyed in Clutch's first phase through items such as ⟦i:496¦Euthanasia⟧ or ⟦p:chaos-card¦Chaos Card⟧, it will automatically be forced into its second phase but without the purple fire places or bone orbitals.
* Clutch can be killed at 50% hp using ⟦i:653¦Vade Retro⟧.
* ⟦i:697¦Vanishing Twin⟧ spawns a second Clutch in its second phase as there are not enough Clickety Clacks.
* ⟦i:291¦Flush!⟧ will convert all Clickety Clacks into poop, immediately starting the second phase.
* Items like ⟦i:596¦Uranus⟧ and ⟦i:608¦Freezer Baby⟧ allow the Clickety Clacks to be frozen and destroyed, giving an easier time with the battle.
* The ⟦i:285¦D10⟧ will downgrade the Clickety Clacks into Globins and start the second phase.
* Using ⟦i:631¦Meat Cleaver⟧ isn't recommended until the second phase of the fight, as it will also split the invulnerable Clickety Clacks.

bosses.behavior:
Colostomia alternates between the following attacks:
* Hops in place and then slides toward Isaac in the closest cardinal direction, firing projectiles in both perpendicular directions as she moves and leaving trails of explosive gas.
** The slide can be at a slight angle if Isaac isn't perfectly aligned with it.
** Colostomia continuously performs this attack until ~40% of the room is covered in explosive gas.
* Launches a ⟦i:209¦Butt Bombs⟧ Bomb towards Isaac that ignites any gas clouds its explosion hits, causing a chain of explosions.
** This is always her first attack upon spawning.
** Unlike Isaac's Butt Bombs, these do not fog the room.
After dropping to half health, the bag containing Colostomia explodes, creating explosive clouds and leaving her adhering to the floor.
* Jumps to another nearby location, firing 8 projectiles in a radial burst and creating a puddle of harmful Brown Creep where she lands.
** Only 2 puddles of Brown Creep can persist at once.
* Spits two ⟦i:209¦Butt Bombs⟧ Bombs at Isaac. The range of these bombs is dependent on how close Isaac is to her.
* Farts, creating a ring of explosive gas around her location.

bosses.behavior:
* Charges horizontally off-screen. Reappears alongside 7-8 copies of himself from the opposite end of the screen. These copies are randomly dispersed, covering a majority of the screen and will continuing charging. After all the copies have charged off-screen, the original Conquest will charge back into the room.
** He performs this attack more often if Isaac is to his left or right.
** All copies of Conquest share his health bar.
* Fires 4 homing projectiles in the cardinal directions.
* Ascends off-screen and summons 8-10 staggered ⟦i:160¦Crack the Sky⟧ beams in random locations.
** Returns from the side of the screen.
Conquest deals a whole heart of contact damage, including every summoned copy during his charge.

bosses.behavior:
Daddy Long Legs' head hangs down stationary and can perform the following attacks:
* Raises his head, making it invulnerable, and stomps the ground in random locations around the room 4 times in quick succession. ⟨24⟩ One of these legs will always stomp on top of Isaac's position.
** The appendages that he stomps with can be attacked to damage him.
* Lifts his head off-screen and stomps the ground 4 times at regular intervals on top of Isaac's position. At the end of the 4 stomps, he slams his head down quickly, shooting out 8 projectiles in all directions. He can only slam his head down along a horizontal plane across the center of the room and slams it down close to Isaac's position.
** Occasionally performs a fifth stomp before slamming his head down.
** The appendages that he stomps with can be attacked to damage him.
* Spits out 2-3 Spiders.
** These spiders can be killed by Daddy Long Legs' stomps and head slam.
Daddy Long Legs' foot stomp and head slam deal a whole heart of contact damage.
bosses.notes:
* The passive item ⟦i:170¦Daddy Longlegs⟧ is a familiar form of this boss, stomping enemies to assist Isaac. The familiar will even attack the Daddy Long Legs.
* On rooms where Daddy Long Legs is treated as a degraded Boss, they can be used to blow open doors.
* ⟨7⟩ Like ⟦e:mom¦Mom⟧'s stomp, his stomp deals explosive damage.

bosses.behavior:
* Fires three projectiles towards Isaac.
* Whistles before summoning 1-3 Brownie Corns and then fires 3 projectiles at Isaac.
* Quickly performs 2 long dashes towards Isaac while bouncing off obstacles and walls, after which he pauses to catch his breath. While dashing, he leaves slippery Brown Creep.
** Occasionally spawns a Corn Mine at the start of a dash, which immediately detonates, poisoning Dangle. If he is poisoned while dashing he leaves behind damaging Green Creep instead.
** Brownie Corns caught in his dashes are knocked back a distance.
bosses.notes:
* ⟨24⟩ Dangle is much less common than his counterpart, ⟦e:dingle¦Dingle⟧, spawning only 1/4th as often.
* If a ⟦i:209¦Butt Bombs⟧ Bomb goes off in the same room as Dangle, it will heal him.
** ⟨28⟩ Butt Bomb effect on ⟦i:52¦Dr. Fetus⟧ or ⟦i:168¦Epic Fetus⟧ does not heal Dangle.
* ⟦i:291¦Flush!⟧ kills Dangle instantly and causes him to leave behind 6 Brownie Corns.

bosses.strategy:
Throughout the majority of a run, Tainted Jacob is harassed by Dark Esau with no intended way of permanently getting rid of him. Because of this, playing as Tainted Jacob requires the player to manage both the playable Jacob and his vengeful brother Esau.
* Using ⟦i:722¦Anima Sola⟧ is key to success for Tainted Jacob, as it can help prevent damage from Dark Esau or turn him into a powerful weapon against enemies.
* In the ⟦s:mines¦Mines⟧, Tainted Jacob can intentionally run into Dark Esau in order to abuse the mechanics of The Lost form (specifically Flight in an area which normally removes any previous sources of flight you may have attained) to quickly and easily acquire the ⟦i:627¦Knife Piece 2⟧ with a rapid and flight-assisted escape if you are attempting to reach the ⟦s:corpse¦Corpse⟧ to defeat ⟦e:mother¦Mother⟧.
** Typically, the escape path would become excessively difficult due to both ⟦e:mother-s-shadow¦Mother's Shadow⟧ and Dark Esau attempting to charge at you in intervals which are typically out of sync, making it very difficult to escape without taking damage or potentially dying.
** By remaining in The Lost form, this also allows you bypass the damage which would normally be required to enter the door in order to advance to ⟦s:mausoleum¦Mausoleum⟧ / ⟦s:gehenna¦Gehenna⟧.
** It is recommended to fully clear the floor first, as Tainted Jacob remains in The Lost form until the next floor is reached.
* While in his Lost form, Tainted Jacob can take Devil Deals in the same way as the Lost. At the end of each floor with a Devil Deal spawn, it is possible to intentionally have Dark Esau turn Tainted Jacob into The Lost form in order to receive free Devil Deals.
* Items and transformations that give you flight (, , , and ) to be able to more easily dodge Dark Esau in rooms with pits and rocks, and/or spectral tears (quicker room clears with obstacles plus can cheese obstacle mechanics with Dark Esau) can help quickly clear rooms and avoid the brother's attacks.
* ⟦t:145¦Perfection⟧ is not lost upon getting hit by Dark Esau.
* It can actually be quite risky to take ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧. Each Dark Esau can charge in a different direction than the other, which ultimately increases your chances of getting hit by one of them.
Dark Esau himself should be respected. Being touched a single time by Dark Esau has a high chance of leading to a run's end by putting Jacob in his fragile Lost state for the remainder of a floor.
* Dark Esau deals no contact damage to Jacob while chained down with Anima Sola.
* Dark Esau's touch effect can be avoided while shielded, invulnerable, or otherwise immune to damage (such as with ⟦i:313¦Holy Mantle⟧ or ⟦i:210¦Gnawed Leaf⟧).
* Dark Esau keeps a consistent distance from Jacob, and will only charge if he is within this distance. Dark Esau will never actually be able to touch Jacob unless he starts his charge animation, charges, or Jacob runs into him.
** As such, running from and maintaining enough distance from Dark Esau will prevent him from charging.
** In some cases such as being next to an obstacle, Dark Esau will stop moving within the prop and will be unable to charge until Jacob moves away from it.
** Dark Esau will only charge at Jacob once he enters his cardinal line of sight. Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he is positioned diagonally from him, even if Jacob is standing still.
* Dark Esau's position at all times is determined by his position relative to the general layout of the floor, meaning he persists in the same location even when Tainted Jacob moves through rooms. Entering a new room cancels Esau's charge if he was preparing one or frees him if he was bound by Anima Sola.
** Caution should be taken when moving between rooms where Dark Esau is near the doorway, as this may lead to a situation where Tainted Jacob immediately runs into Dark Esau.
** Teleporting a great distance or traveling quickly through rooms with the help of special items or a high speed stat makes it harder for Dark Esau to catch up to Jacob.
** If Dark Esau is in the process of traveling between rooms, it is possible to use Anima Sola to chain him outside of the current area Tainted Jacob is in.
* As Dark Esau takes time to respawn after entering a new floor, the first few seconds on every floor can be used to explore rooms freely.
* Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he eats a Paralysis Pill.
Considering the damage Dark Esau can deal to enemies and the fact that Anima Sola can be canceled early by using it a second time, Dark Esau can become a powerful, albeit dangerous weapon to use against enemies by positioning Tainted Jacob in ways that manipulate him into charging into enemies. This is further compounded, as his charge attack ignores Boss Armor.
* Anima Sola can be used in an empty room to instantly summon Dark Esau in order to use him advantageously.
** Dark Esau's charge is able to single-handedly kill most early bosses in one or two hits. He can also be held in place with Anima Sola to bait chasing enemies, as Jacob can stand behind Dark Esau and cause them to run into him.
* In ⟦s:greed-mode¦Greed Mode⟧, Anima Sola will always be charged at the beginning of a new wave. This can be taken advantage of by binding Dark Esau before a new wave begins and then letting him charge into a freshly spawned enemy group or a priority enemy like a champion. Since releasing Dark Esau manually does not consume the item charge, the item will still be available to restrict him again immediately afterwards.
* Dark Esau's charge will extinguish Fire Places.
* Dark Esau cannot damage friendly enemies.
* When Dark Esau charges while in fear, he charges away from Tainted Jacob.
* Dark Esau cannot affect other players and ignores them completely.
** ⟨15⟩ If multiple players are playing Tainted Jacob, then any Tainted Jacob who touches any Dark Esau will still be turned into a ghost or die. Tainted Jacob players will only be able to use Anima Sola on their own Dark Esau, and if one of the Tainted Jacobs is completely killed, both Dark Esaus will begin to target the one that is still living.
** ⟨15⟩ When Tainted Jacob completely dies and is turned into a small ghost baby as a Co-Op partner, Dark Esau will still follow the ghost of Tainted Jacob if no other Tainted Jacob players are in the match, allowing them to still use him as a high damage weapon to help their teammates.
** ⟨16⟩ Dark Esau will no longer deal damage to enemies or charge at the ghost of Tainted Jacob until he is revived.
* If Tainted Jacob was turned into his ghostly form by Dark Esau, then dying and being revived upon completion of the boss will have him revive as his ghostly form.
** ⟨15⟩ If Tainted Jacob is dead at the start of a floor, Dark Esau will still spawn, but will target one of the living players instead. Unless they are also playing Tainted Jacob, he will never hurt them outside his spawning animation.
** ⟨16⟩ If Tainted Jacob is dead at the end of a floor, he will respawn at the start of the next floor.
* Dark Esau is considered a boss.
** Like every other "boss", Dark Esau can be spawned with debug commands. However, if playing as someone other than Tainted Jacob, the player will be immune to his attacks.
*** ⟦c:jacob¦Jacob⟧, even in his normal non-tainted form, is an exception. When touched by Dark Esau, he will take damage, but will not turn into a ghost. ⟦c:jacob¦Esau⟧, like most characters, is still immune to Dark Esau.
* When the console command "restart 39" is loaded, the player will be spawned as a ghostly version of Tainted Jacob. The only differences is that Dark Esau never seems to spawn and that this version of Tainted Jacob has the health of ⟦c:the-lost¦The Lost⟧.

bosses.behavior:
* Sends out a ring of 12 projectiles.
* If Isaac is below him, fires a ⟦i:118¦Brimstone⟧ laser downwards.
* Charges twice across the screen, veering slowly towards Isaac while charging. When going off-screen, he reappears from the opposite end of the screen. Dark One will do this attack more often if Isaac moves to one of his sides.
* Dims the room, causing the effect for a period of time.
bosses.notes: If Dark One dims the room, pause the game and the dim will eventually go away while still in the pause screen.

bosses.rewards:
⟦i:207¦Ball of Bandages⟧
⟦i:73¦Cube of Meat⟧
⟨16⟩ ⟦t:116¦Locust of Death⟧ (1% chance)
bosses.behavior:
* Spawns four Death Scythes along the walls of the room, aligned with Isaac in the cardinal directions. After a few seconds, they will accelerate towards Isaac.
** If Isaac is close to a wall, the scythe that would normally be spawned on that wall does not spawn.
* Spawns two Death Scythes in random positions around the room that constantly home in on Isaac until they are destroyed.
* Uses ⟦i:66¦The Hourglass⟧ to slow Isaac down.
After enough damage is dealt, Death will dismount from his horse. The horse has 150 HP, but it will also lose health when Death is damaged. Attacking the horse does not damage Death.
* Death occasionally spawns two Knights and can have a maximum of two.
* Death's horse continuously flies horizontally across the room going off-screen and continuing on from the opposite end of the screen.
** Its charging patterns occur along 3 paths, starting with an upper charge into a middle charge a short distance below and finally a lower charge an identical distance below the middle path. It then restarts this process and can perform its upper charge in a new position in the room.
*** Its first charge will always leave room below it to allow for the lower second and third charges.
** The horse continues to charge even after Death has been defeated.
** It deals heavy damage to any enemy it runs into, except Death.
Both Death and his horse deal a whole heart of contact damage in both phases.
bosses.notes: * When Death uses The Hourglass, ⟦i:329¦The Ludovico Technique⟧'s tear is slow to respond and has a higher maximum speed, becoming difficult to control.

bosses.behavior:
Delirium's main form is stationary but teleports erratically around the room and performs the following attacks:
* Continuously sends out various overlapping patterns of white projectiles for the entire duration of the fight:
** 20 projectiles that slowly rotate clockwise or counterclockwise while expanding.
** 16 projectiles outwards in all directions.
** 14 projectiles that rotate clockwise, counterclockwise, or back and forth while expanding.
** 10 projectiles that fluctuate in and out while expanding.
** 8 slow-moving green-tinted ⟦i:149¦Ipecac⟧ projectiles in all directions.
** 6 projectiles that travel outwards in a zig-zag pattern.
** 4 projectiles outwards in a lop-sided cross.
** 4 lines of 3 projectiles that spiral outwards.
** A spread of 5 projectiles in Isaac's direction.
** A burst of projectiles that travel outwards in random directions.
** A stray short-range projectile in a random direction.
*** The projectile size per each attack is random and varies from very small to moderately large.
* Transforms into bosses previously encountered during the run, which can include major bosses such as ⟦e:mom¦Mom⟧ or ⟦e:it-lives¦It Lives!⟧.
** When it transforms into a boss, Delirium retains its own health, not the health of the boss it transformed into.
** When transforming into certain multi-phase bosses, such as Isaac, Delirium copies the phase that that boss would be at, given its current health percentage.
** When transforming into a segmented boss, only the first two segments share Delirium's hp; the other segments have separately generated hp and can be defeated separately.
** In rare occasions, it can transform into two or even three bosses at once.
** In rare occasions, it spawns a separate copy of the boss it transformed into.
** Whether it turns into a Champion variant or a regular variant is random and does not depend on which variant was previously defeated.
** ⟨7⟩ It is unable to properly transform into Hush's true form. In order for this to happen, very few bosses must be encountered in the run. Additionally, many of Hush's attacks do not work properly and the sprite is also unfinished.
** ⟨24⟩ Can transform into ⟦e:baby-plum¦Baby Plum⟧, ⟦e:bumbino¦Bumbino⟧, and ⟦e:the-pile¦The Pile⟧, but only Baby Plum has a unique sprite. Cannot transform into any other Repentance bosses.
** ⟨24⟩ Cannot transform into ⟦e:mega-satan¦Mega Satan⟧, rendering its unique sprite unused.
* Occasionally, it returns to its main form to perform projectile attacks at a faster pace.
* As it takes damage, it becomes more aggressive: moving, teleporting, transforming, and attacking at a faster rate.
** ⟨16⟩ ⟦e:mom¦Mom⟧ and ⟦e:satan¦Satan⟧'s second phase are exempt from the faster attack speed, instead attacking at a fixed speed.
** It also takes on a reddish hue to signify this change.
** Destroying non-Delirium segments when it transforms into segmented bosses can also temporarily trigger this effect.
** If Delirium is being dealt damage at a significantly high rate from multiple tear sources, it will attack, teleport, and transform at extreme speeds.
Upon defeat, the screen starts to glitch, fills with static, and the room switches between different environments, while short scenes from the current run are played ending with Delirium screaming and bursting into a small puddle of blood.
bosses.notes:
* Delirium is immune to ⟦p:chaos-card¦Chaos Card⟧.
* Upon defeating Delirium, Isaac gains 2 charges for his active item.
* ⟦i:475¦Plan C⟧ can be used to kill Delirium. After Plan C is used against Delirium, when pausing in the instant of each flash from Delirium's death animation, the animation can be skipped before the death from Plan C's 3 seconds delay; this works because each flash from Delirium's death animation is still played when the game is paused. It is also recommended to position Isaac on the chest spawn location before Plan C's death occurs.
** It works with ⟦i:332¦Lazarus' Rags⟧, as it revives Isaac on the spot. However, the Completion Mark will go towards Lazarus, not the character originally selected.
** ⟨24⟩ ⟦p:soul-of-lazarus¦Soul of Lazarus⟧ and ⟦i:688¦Inner Child⟧ revive Isaac in the same room he died in, and the Completion Mark goes toward the selected/current character.
** ⟨24⟩ While playing as ⟦c:tainted-lost¦Tainted Lost⟧, ⟦i:619¦Birthright⟧ revives him inside Delirium's room without transforming himself into another character.
** ⟨16⟩ This is no longer necessary, as ⟦i:475¦Plan C⟧ will kill Isaac in 10 seconds after being used inside Delirium's room, which is enough time to let its death animation finish, and reward the completion mark for the current character before Isaac's Last Will pops up.
* Most entities that are considered to be bosses by the game (usually identified by ones that add the boss health bar to the screen, though there are exceptions) are marked as bosses that Delirium can transform into.
* Delirium's transformations have a huge amount of quirks and odd mechanics, and as such are practically impossible to fully document. A good amount of these quirks are documented below.
** Delirium can transform into either form of ⟦e:satan¦Satan⟧.
** When transformed into the ⟦e:gurglings¦Gurglings⟧ or the ⟦e:turdlings¦Turdlings⟧, it only appears as one instead of two.
** When transformed into ⟦e:headless-horseman¦Headless Horseman⟧, it transforms into either the head or the body, but it doesn't transform into both at the same time.
** If Delirium transforms into ⟦e:isaac¦Isaac⟧ and Delirium's health is low enough, it will attempt to perform Isaac's ⟦i:160¦Crack the Sky⟧ attack. However, because Delirium's boss arena is a quadruple-sized room, the attack will cover half of the arena, making it extremely deadly.
** Each size of ⟦e:fistula¦Fistula⟧ and ⟦e:teratoma¦Teratoma⟧ count as a separate boss, which Delirium can transform into just like any other boss.
** This also results in many bugs due to unaccounted for transformations. These can be viewed in the bugs section of this page.
** When transformed into two instances of the same boss (like ⟦e:lokii¦Lokii⟧ or ⟦e:sisters-vis¦Sisters Vis⟧), one of them can be killed but the other cannot (until Delirium's hp fully runs out).
*** If Delirium transforms into Pink Champion ⟦e:monstro¦Monstro⟧, it only takes the form of one and summons an extra Pink Champion Monstro.
**** This is also true for Pink Champion ⟦e:polycephalus¦Polycephalus⟧ and Pink Champion ⟦e:the-cage¦The Cage⟧.
*** If Delirium transforms into ⟦e:the-lamb¦The Lamb⟧'s second phase then undergoes another transformation, the body doesn't disappear and can be killed, just like the original Lamb's body.
**** Killing this body will cause the screen to become darker for a period of time, just like when you kill the original Lamb's body.
**** Delirium can also transform into the Lamb's body on its own. If this happens, the body disappears when Delirium transforms again.
** When transformed into a boss that has multiple segments, the extra segments can be killed. The head, however, cannot.
*** This also applies to ⟦e:gemini¦Gemini⟧ — Suture can be killed but Contusion cannot.
**** If Delirium transforms into Gemini, then undergoes another transformation, Suture doesn't disappear. Instead, he continues to chase Isaac as if Contusion was killed in the original fight.
** Delirium's ⟦e:mom¦Mom⟧ form only stomps and does not spawn enemies.
* ⟨24⟩ If a segmented worm-boss such as ⟦e:larry-jr¦Larry Jr.⟧ or ⟦e:scolex¦Scolex⟧ is removed via ⟦i:638¦Eraser⟧, Delirium will disappear if it attempts to turn into that boss. This will spawn the ending chest and count as having defeated Delirium. Other multipart bosses' erased pieces may be unable to spawn, but do not kill Delirium entirely.
* ⟨7⟩ If Delirium transforms into Mega Satan, the boss maintains the ability to spawn the Harbingers, the Super Sins, and the Fallen Angels, and can do so in quick succession depending on Delirium's health. This can make the fight much longer, as attacking the bosses spawned by Delirium will have no effect on Delirium's actual health.
* Delirium can transform into Fallen ⟦e:uriel¦Uriel⟧ and Fallen ⟦e:gabriel¦Gabriel⟧ but they don't have unique Delirium skins.
* Each time Delirium transforms, its Status Effect timer resets, allowing for useful effects to be active for a large portion of the fight if re-inflicted frequently enough.
** This quirk is especially useful in conjunction with the petrification from ⟦i:110¦Mom's Contacts⟧, as it can hold Delirium in place each time it is petrified, making it a much easier target to hit.
bosses.strategy:
* Just like with ⟦e:hush¦Hush⟧, effects that cause long-lasting mass slowdown such as ⟦i:232¦Stop Watch⟧ or the I'm Drowsy pill are very valuable, aiding the player's ability to dodge the complex tear patterns and deal with the massive spawns of enemies, which can happen in quick succession.
* ⟨24⟩ ⟦i:514¦Broken Modem⟧ can also remove a lot of bullets, making it a must-have against Delirium.
* Delirium's main form lacks any damage scaling or armor, allowing the opportunity to deal high damage attacks against its massive base HP. Be wary that dealing significant bursts of damage against Delirium will also quickly increase its aggressiveness.
* One may wish to save this fight with ⟦c:tainted-eden¦Tainted Eden⟧ for the last mark of a file, as can make I AM ERROR and Secret Rooms worse.

bosses.behavior:
Dingle remains stationary and performs the following attacks:
* Fires 3 projectiles towards Isaac.
* Whistles before summoning 1-3 Dips and then fires 3 projectiles at Isaac.
* Quickly performs 3 long dashes towards Isaac while bouncing off obstacles and walls, after which he pauses to catch his breath.
** Dips caught in his dashes are knocked back a distance.
** Occasionally, Dingle will leave behind a Poop while using this attack.
bosses.notes:
* ⟦i:291¦Flush!⟧ kills Dingle instantly and causes him to leave behind 6 Dips.
* If a Bomb from ⟦i:209¦Butt Bombs⟧ goes off in the same room as Dingle, it will heal him. ⟨30⟩ This is especially bad if Isaac happens to have ⟦i:378¦No. 2⟧, which causes him to drop butt bombs while firing tears.
** ⟨28⟩ Butt Bombs fired by ⟦i:52¦Dr. Fetus⟧ and ⟦i:168¦Epic Fetus⟧ do not heal Dingle.

source.source: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki (wiki.gg) — CC BY-SA 4.0

bosses.behavior:
In its first phase, Dogma is attached to a television. Damage can only be dealt to Dogma by damaging the television in the center of the room. Any attacks towards Dogma itself causes a shield to briefly appear and block the attack. Dogma moves slowly towards Isaac, leaving a trail of damaging Static Creep and has a variety of attacks:
* Fires three consecutive radial bursts of 8 ⟦i:331¦Godhead⟧ projectiles. If Isaac stands within the projectiles' auras for long enough, a ⟦i:160¦Crack the Sky⟧ beam hits Isaac from above.
* Fires four consecutive bursts of projectiles in groups of 1, 2, 3, and 4 in each of the cardinal directions, with the overall pattern resembling a star.
** Occasionally after firing the 4th burst, Dogma greatly slows down all the projectiles mid-flight, leaving them to float around slowly for a moment before vanishing.
*** Dogma starts using this variant after losing around 60% of its HP, and performs it more frequently the lower its HP is.
* Fires 3 consecutive waves of 3 to 4 projectiles each in random directions. When these projectiles land, it creates thin, harmless rays that point towards Isaac and become damaging lasers after a few seconds.
* Fires a static ⟦i:118¦Brimstone⟧ beam that bends towards Isaac. This beam is always fired in the closest cardinal direction to Isaac and switches if Isaac moves closer to a different cardinal direction.
After destroying the television, Dogma falls apart into a puddle of static, before rising out of it as an orb and growing two pairs of wings resembling a Seraph. During this phase, Dogma continues to chase Isaac between attacks, but becomes vulnerable and has completely different attacks:
* Fires a spread of disorganized feather projectiles towards Isaac if he's to its left or right.
* Summons a ball of light overhead which creates 16 to 18 harmless rays of light that point outwards and spin around the ball in random directions. After a few seconds, the rays stop moving and become damaging thin beams, similar to the ones used by the ⟦e:gabriel¦Angel⟧s. This pattern is repeated three times, then Dogma throws it, firing one last wave of 8 wider beams in the cardinal and ordinal directions before dissipating.
** If the thrown ball of beams is slowed (by ⟦i:232¦Stop Watch⟧ for instance), the 8 beams fire before being properly aligned.
* Turns into a winged wheel resembling an Ophanim and floats off-screen before charging back towards Isaac, continuing off-screen releasing a radial burst with three layers of feather projectiles with 12 feathers each near the end of the dash. It repeats this attack a total of 6 times.
As Dogma takes more and more damage during this phase, its Seraph form will occasionally flicker into various other forms; these include Isaac's head, a lamb's skull with a serpent in its eye, a fly, and a troll face with horns (each of which represents one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse). This is a purely visual effect.
When Dogma's HP reaches zero for the second time, it is destroyed as the whole screen fades to white before turning off like an old TV. Then Isaac is automatically given ⟦i:633¦Dogma⟧ as the cutscene that introduces ⟦e:the-beast¦The Beast⟧ is played.
bosses.notes:
* After the beginning cutscene, Dogma appears very close to Isaac, making it easy to immediately take damage.
* Having a high speed is highly recommended for the second phase, as the charge attack can be almost unavoidable with low speed.
* ⟦i:387¦Censer⟧ makes the second phase more difficult by reducing the space between feathers during Dogma's charging attack while not slowing Dogma itself. It is not recommended for this fight.
* If a ⟦i:331¦Godhead⟧-like projectile is "caught" with ⟦i:522¦Telekinesis⟧, it will be impossible to avoid the projectile's aura. As a result, taking damage is unavoidable.
* As the Dogma room is not counted as a Boss room, effects like ⟦i:535¦Blanket⟧ will not occur in this fight.
* If Isaac has triggered the beginning cutscene, re-entering the room by any means (such as being revived outside the room as ⟦c:bluebaby¦???⟧ with ⟦i:161¦Ankh⟧) will trigger the Dogma fight immediately.
* Before beginning the fight, going out and back into the living-room repeatedly while holding a trinket like ⟦t:32¦Liberty Cap⟧ guarantees to get the best possible effect sooner or later, which can greatly help during the fight.
* ⟦i:632¦Evil Charm⟧ will prevent Isaac from being affected by Dogma's ⟦i:331¦Godhead⟧ aura projectile attack in its first phase.
* Any effect that lasts for one room won't remain after the fight and won't carry over to the Ultra Harbingers and The Beast fight.
* ⟦t:145¦Perfection⟧ will spawn after defeating Dogma if the correct conditions are met, however, the trinket will be left behind when Isaac arrives to fight the Ultra Harbingers and The Beast.

bosses.behavior:
* Envy floats around the room diagonally, bouncing off the walls.
* He splits into 2 medium heads upon death which split into 2 small heads each when destroyed. These small heads split one last time into 2 even smaller heads when destroyed.
** The last head killed drops a Troll Bomb or ⟦i:49¦Shoop da Whoop!⟧.
* The heads increase in speed as they split into smaller versions.
bosses.notes:
* ⟨6⟩ Occasionally, 2 regular Envies appear in a Mini-Boss Room and the boss message will display "Isaac vs. ⟦e:super-envy¦Super Envy⟧".
* ⟨28⟩ Both Envy and Super Envy are extremely vulnerable to ⟦i:466¦Contagion⟧ as their relatively low health generally ensures that the poison effect will persist all the way down to the smallest heads.
* ⟨7⟩ Envy can drop ⟦i:49¦Shoop da Whoop!⟧ even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

bosses.behavior:
* If Isaac is to the left or right of Famine, he charges horizontally across the screen. He continues this charge off-screen and reappears from the opposite end of the screen.
* Spawns a Pooter with a limit of 2.
** If this limit is reached Famine will move to try to position himself horizontally of Isaac so he can charge at him.
** Any Pooters caught in Famine's charge will be killed.
When Famine takes a sufficient amount of damage, his body and horse explode and vanish while only his head remains.
* Famine's head behaves similarly to a Maw, slowly moving towards Isaac, and occasionally stops to fire three projectiles in a spread at Isaac.
Famine deals a whole heart of contact damage in both phases and during his charge.

bosses.behavior:
* Moves around the room slowly, bouncing off the walls.
* When enough health is depleted, the one large Fistula breaks into four medium Fistulas.
** Medium forms behave identically but move slightly faster and can bounce off other enemies.
* Each of the four medium Fistulas breaks into two small Fistulas.
** Small forms behave identically but move very fast.
* Each of the smallest Fistulas spawns a Charger with 15 health points on defeat unless they are over a pit or other obstacle.
* Altogether, the pieces have a combined total of 184 HP (304 HP if including the 8 Chargers).
* All stages of Fistula deal a whole heart of contact damage.

bosses.notes:
* The angels will always alternate in order of appearance. Thus, if Uriel has just been defeated, the next angel spawn is guaranteed to be Gabriel and vice versa.
* If the player defeats an angel, and they already have both Key Pieces, no Key Piece drops. However, if this occurs, it counts as a normal room clear, and the player may be rewarded with a pickup or chest.
* Angels only drop a Key Piece the first time they are defeated, even if Isaac does not pick up the Key Piece, subsequent kills in the same run provide no pedestal item rewards.
** ⟨28⟩ Angels will drop a Key Piece even if they were defeated before. Additionally, if Isaac has one of the Key Pieces, angels will always drop the other piece, even if he already skipped that piece or that particular angel normally wouldn't drop it (for instance, Uriel will drop Key Piece 2 if Isaac already has Key Piece 1 from fighting him earlier).
* Rerolling ⟦i:238¦Key Piece 1⟧ or ⟦i:239¦Key Piece 2⟧ will yield an item from a pool, depending on which room the Key Pieces are in.
** Rerolling the Key Pieces in an Angel Room will yield an item from the Angel Room item pool.
* The angel's beams of light are rendered at a height, though their hitbox is on the ground (and their shadow is invisible). For diagonal beams, this causes Isaac to take damage even if he is below them, and allows him to partially walk into the beams if he is above them.
* ⟨28⟩ Angels will drop items from the Angel Room item pool instead of the Key Pieces if Isaac is holding ⟦t:123¦Filigree Feather⟧.
* ⟨28⟩ Sometimes, two angel statues can appear in the same room. Destroying both at the same time will spawn both Uriel and Gabriel, but only one Key Piece will drop. If each angel is spawned and defeated separately, both will drop Key Pieces.
** ⟨24⟩ Both angels will drop key pieces if fought at the same time.
* Uriel and Gabriel are immune to the Fear effect.
* When spawned inside a Sacrifice Room, the room is not locked, allowing Isaac to simply walk out of the fight.
** When returning to the Sacrifice Room, the angel will be gone.
** ⟨3⟩ As a result, it is possible to miss obtaining ⟦i:238¦Key Piece 1⟧ while getting ⟦i:239¦Key Piece 2⟧.

bosses.behavior:
Gemini starts as a pair of bosses connected together by an umbilical cord.
* Contusion chases Isaac and periodically charges increasing his speed, but stops to catch his breath afterwards.
* Suture, while attached to Contusion, shoots a projectile towards Isaac if not behind an obstacle.
* If Contusion is killed first, Suture detaches and begins charging furiously at Isaac. He has high momentum and takes extra knock-back from tears, which can cause him to gain speed.
** If Suture is killed first, there is no change to Contusion's behavior.
bosses.notes:
* Status effects will equally affect both Contusion and Suture even if it was only applied to one of them. This includes effects granting knockback such as ⟦i:637¦Knockout Drops⟧.
** This also applies to Green Champion Gemini, despite the twins being completely separated entities.

source.source: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki (wiki.gg) — CC BY-SA 4.0

bosses.behavior:
* Makes short hops towards Isaac, similar to ⟦e:monstro¦Monstro⟧.
* Fires a black ⟦i:149¦Ipecac⟧ shot towards Isaac, leaving a large puddle of Black Creep on impact.
* Leaps off-screen and lands on Isaac's position twice in a row, similar to ⟦e:monstro-ii¦Monstro II⟧.
** Leaves a large puddle of Black Creep on his first landing.
*** The Black Creep spawned by Gish's first jump will remain for the entire battle until Gish is killed.
** Spawns two Clots on his second landing.
*** There is a maximum of 2 Clots alive at once.
*** Gish deals a full heart of contact damage.
bosses.notes:
* ⟨24⟩ While just as common as other bosses in the Dank Depths' boss pool, Gish is only 1/4th as common as other Boss Room bosses in The Depths.
** Gish is the only boss to have more than 1 boss weight besides ⟦e:the-matriarch¦The Matriarch⟧.
* Gish will often be accompanied by Clots.

bosses.behavior:
Gluttony wanders randomly around the room and performs one of two attacks:
* Shoots 8 projectiles in all directions.
* Fires a ⟦i:118¦Brimstone⟧ laser from his belly towards Isaac if he is aligned in a cardinal direction.
Gluttony deals a whole heart of contact damage.
bosses.notes:
* ⟨6⟩ Occasionally, 2 regular Gluttonies appear in a Mini-Boss Room and the boss message will display "Isaac vs ⟦e:super-gluttony¦Super Gluttony⟧".
* ⟨7⟩ Gluttony can drop ⟦i:15¦<3⟧ even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

source.source: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki (wiki.gg) — CC BY-SA 4.0

bosses.behavior:
Great Gideon is always fought in a vertical double-size room and has no health in a traditional sense. Instead, Isaac must battle 6 waves of monsters to beat him, similar to ⟦s:greed-mode¦Greed Mode⟧ waves. Each wave begins once all enemies from the previous wave have been defeated.
He uses the following attacks during these waves:
* Creates a vacuum that affects the whole room, pulling in Isaac and all monsters and monster projectiles. It also pulls in additional rock projectiles. Touching Gideon while he is performing this attack damages Isaac.
* Spits 5 projectiles in a cone shape towards Isaac. The center projectile is larger and splits into 8 projectiles in a radial burst when it lands or hits something.
* Charges up then spits large flame projectiles down the center of the arena that can occasionally leave small fires behind.
** Some enemies caught in this attack are turned into their flaming versions: Rock Spider into Coal Spider, Clotty into Grilled Clotty and Gyro into Grilled Gyro.
* After the beginning of the 4th wave, Great Gideon charges up and releases a rock wave down the center of the room, breaking parts of the floor and leaving gaps.
** There is always at least 1 gap between the trail of holes created by this attack as to not completely trap Isaac on either end of the room.
* Gideon does not spawn the next enemy wave during the middle of any of his attacks and only progresses a wave once he has finished.
After Isaac defeats all 6 waves of monsters, Great Gideon will deactivate, similar to a regular Stone Grimace.
bosses.notes:
* Great Gideon can be instantly killed with ⟦p:chaos-card¦Chaos Card⟧. Doing so reveals a unique 1x2 Crawl Space beneath him, containing two locked chests, two items and a random key.
** This can be done at any time, even if he has already been defeated, as his deactivated body still remains after returning to the room.
** Defeating Great Gideon in this way plays a unique animation in which the Chaos Card gets lodged in his forehead before he explodes.
** Pressing on a Kill Plate in the room similarly kills Great Gideon, and reveals the unique 1x2 Crawl Space. This also plays the unique animation of the ⟦p:chaos-card¦Chaos Card⟧ in his head. Doing so is possible with ⟦i:386¦D12⟧
* Completing waves will not charge active items.
* ⟦i:697¦Vanishing Twin⟧ will duplicate Great Gideon and increase the number of waves by 2. The waves themselves contain no extra enemies.
* Great Gideon can be fought outside the ⟦s:mines¦Mines⟧ or the ⟦s:ashpit¦Ashpit⟧ via using a ⟦p:iv-the-emperor-reversed¦IV - The Emperor?⟧ card in ⟦s:downpour¦Downpour⟧ or ⟦s:dross¦Dross⟧. If encountered outside his regular stages, he has preset waves consisting of Frowning Gapers, Wall Creeps, Round Worms, Gurgles, and Suckers.
